body:
This pull request updates several dependencies and configuration settings related to GitHub Actions workflows and pre-commit hooks, focusing on keeping action references up-to-date, improving compatibility, and removing unused hooks. The most important changes are grouped below by theme.

**Dependency Updates (GitHub Actions):**
* Updated `github/codeql-action` references to v4.31.7 across multiple workflow and action files for improved security and bug fixes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-96c941d62860ad493e2ef6e2e641b5cdda1373729143a0a72a44f11f46895e4dL77-R84) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e3935040aa017c086385661529a7cfa1428d60d5161a727d1872411a898b1490L76-R76) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-29d14f63e8e2bccda34701dbb3c8843946efc8e7060dc14932e6650d44e98252L133-R133) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-f3f51df6fb11570f760570da5b8a73b499883de668cde9b62490c926926a702fL334-R334) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-e219d1eac78ac47645c01f20f84695ee9d5e83232df177d89493166799da8cd7L189-R189) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-e219d1eac78ac47645c01f20f84695ee9d5e83232df177d89493166799da8cd7L202-R207) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-10424e768fe9e0c99e40920fd09fd11f6edc765df5cd2a54bf0d2633417527abL460-R460) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-c38ff650d22521ddd1a24fbbf07f784a6e9583a75cdc3ddfe4dadf59c0aa802bL417-R417) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-99cde55d7cefa820f0cb01d50c02927e72c3b2d76fab222cdd499b5cc7e1bfe9L209-R209)
* Updated `actions/setup-node` to v6.1.0 in several workflows and custom actions to ensure the latest Node.js setup features and compatibility. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-780c41a378f1aca96db8e87ec23ad964555bee09f8ed8e5a867bbf0505c4446aL34-R34) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f3f51df6fb11570f760570da5b8a73b499883de668cde9b62490c926926a702fL184-R184) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-10424e768fe9e0c99e40920fd09fd11f6edc765df5cd2a54bf0d2633417527abL291-R291) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-6109a8dbedc5762a599893233286d8887ec7285038cd020bfd5e4f5a8b7694c6L124-R124) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-b14a7c3a3c2d6f20a9283b6b4d427d58d55c37947b7e7babf51f5d5d7ee15b40L125-R121)
* Updated `peter-evans/create-pull-request` to v7.0.11 for enhanced pull request creation features and bug fixes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-12fc5ceadd74bafdd93b9915fab461a06281f752338b8ed4e9dd908437734753L52-R52) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b4ca036af55cd0a5cef425f25bacc09f094dc8659d1a60e1a69df6e28fc44107L166-R166)

**Workflow and Configuration Changes:**
* Removed the unused `renovate-config-validator` pre-commit hook from `.pre-commit-config.yaml` to streamline pre-commit checks.
* Updated other action references to their latest patch versions for improved stability, including `softprops/action-gh-release`, `actions/stale`, `sigstore/cosign-installer`, and `github/issue-metrics`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-87db21a973eed4fef5f32b267aa60fcee5cbdf03c67fafdc2a9b553bb0b15f34L20-R20) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b5e0854ed0838024d5cc25b4e030922e34648b9ea8c432807e35495fb805b894L28-R28) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d462aa6948ef2a3f62e8f193749ea6eddd4f80f0000f17259470d5d0a06ae35bL566-R566) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-058915769a1a187c73ce1e7dec61087658f3b4d192a808b693d232f81b9d5f80L33-R33)

**Workflow Logic Adjustments (PR Lint):**
* Changed default Python and Go versions used in PR linting to Python 3.14 and Go 1.25, respectively, to match latest language releases. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b14a7c3a3c2d6f20a9283b6b4d427d58d55c37947b7e7babf51f5d5d7ee15b40L385-R381) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b14a7c3a3c2d6f20a9283b6b4d427d58d55c37947b7e7babf51f5d5d7ee15b40L522-R518)
* Set `VALIDATE_ALL_CODEBASE` to `false` by default, reducing unnecessary codebase-wide validation on push events.
* Removed logic for applying and committing linter fixes automatically, including related environment variable exports and pull request creation steps, simplifying the workflow. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b14a7c3a3c2d6f20a9283b6b4d427d58d55c37947b7e7babf51f5d5d7ee15b40L685-L691) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b14a7c3a3c2d6f20a9283b6b4d427d58d55c37947b7e7babf51f5d5d7ee15b40L702-L810)

**Minor Version Reference Simplifications:**
* Standardized the use of version references for `actions/github-script` to use `@v8` instead of `@v8.0.0` for consistency and future-proofing. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8b0d23f7a2ed3780b1fa5fec5c1e2988ba73c10b4316941163ad7a018e80c11dL51-R51) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-96c941d62860ad493e2ef6e2e641b5cdda1373729143a0a72a44f11f46895e4dL77-R84) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-12fc5ceadd74bafdd93b9915fab461a06281f752338b8ed4e9dd908437734753L79-R79)

Overall, these changes ensure that CI/CD workflows are using the latest stable versions of their dependencies, remove unused configuration, and streamline the PR lint workflow for maintainability.

body: Fixes deployment failures caused by deleting target directories before uploading files. The workflow was running `rm -rf web/*` which removed the `/opt/propertyhub/web/` directory structure, then `scp` would fail because the target directories no longer existed. This replaces the manual cleanup with `rsync --delete`, which: - Creates directories automatically as needed - Syncs only changed files (more efficient) - Automatically removes orphaned/old files on the server via the `--delete` flag - Eliminates the "No such file or directory" scp error Removed the entire "Cleaning deployment target" SSH block and replaced the scp commands for web/templates and web/static with rsync equivalents.

body:
Domains protected by Cloudflare (e.g., npmjs.com) return 403 errors when checking multiple links rapidly, causing false positives.

## Changes

- **Rate limiting per domain** (`rateLimitPerDomain` option): Configurable minimum delay between requests to the same hostname. Implemented with domain-specific queue using iterative processing to avoid stack overflow.

- **Status code allowlist** (`allowStatusCodes` option): Pattern-based mapping to treat specific status codes as valid for certain domains. E.g., `{ "npmjs\\.com": [403] }` accepts 403 from npmjs.com.

- **Browser-like headers**: User-Agent set to Chrome 131 with standard browser headers (`accept-language`, `sec-fetch-*`) to reduce bot detection.

## Example

```js
{
  "markdown-links/no-dead-urls": ["error", {
    "rateLimitPerDomain": 1500,           // 1.5s between requests to same domain
    "allowStatusCodes": {
      "npmjs\\.com": [403]                 // Treat npmjs.com 403 as valid
    }
  }]
}
```

Both options default to disabled (0/empty) for backward compatibility.

body:
Documents the zone definition system architecture: JSON-based static entity definitions loaded by both server and client via shared library.

## Changes

- **New section** after Entity-System documenting zone definition architecture
- **Entity ID ranges**: Players (1-999), Static Entities (1000-1999), Mobs (2000-2999), Reserved (3000+)
- **Data format decisions**: JSON in `/data/zones/*.zone.json`, shared DTOs in `Mmo.Shared.Zones`, unified `ZoneDefinitionLoader`
- **Implementation examples**: C# loader class and usage patterns for server/client

## Structure Example

```
ZoneDefinition
├── ZoneId (string)
├── ZoneName (string)
├── Bounds (MinX, MaxX, MinY, MaxY)
├── SpawnPoints[] (Id, X, Y, Type, IsDefault)
└── StaticEntities[] (Id, Type, X, Y, Properties)
```

## JSON Example

```json
{
  "zoneId": "startzone",
  "staticEntities": [
    {
      "id": 1000,
      "type": "Door",
      "properties": {
        "targetZone": "Hauptstadt",
        "targetSpawn": "from-startzone"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Updated table of contents to reflect new section ordering.

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Aufgabe

Füge einen neuen Abschnitt **"Zone-Definition & Statische Entities"** in `docs/TECHNICAL_DESIGN.md` hinzu.

Der Abschnitt soll nach dem bestehenden Abschnitt "Entity-System" (Zeile ~305) eingefügt werden.

## Inhalt des neuen Abschnitts

```markdown
---

## Zone-Definition & Statische Entities

Zone-Definitionen beschreiben alle statischen Entities einer Zone (Türen, Portale, Kisten, Schilder, NPCs, Spawnpoints). Diese werden als **JSON-Dateien** gespeichert und von Server UND Client über die `Mmo.Shared` Library geladen.

### Datenformat-Entscheidungen

| Aspekt | Entscheidung | Begründung |
|--------|--------------|------------|
| **Format** | JSON | Menschenlesbar, versionierbar in Git |
| **Speicherort** | `/data/zones/*.zone.json` | Zentral, von Server + Client nutzbar |
| **Shared DTOs** | `Mmo.Shared.Zones` Namespace | Keine Duplikation |
| **Loader** | `ZoneDefinitionLoader` (Shared) | Einheitliche Ladelogik |

### Entity-ID Bereiche

| Bereich | Verwendung |
|---------|------------|
| 1 - 999 | Player (auto-increment) |
| 1000 - 1999 | Statische Entities (Türen, Portale, Kisten, Signs) |
| 2000 - 2999 | Dynamische Mobs |
| 3000+ | Reserviert für zukünftige Erweiterungen |

### Zone-Definition Struktur

```
ZoneDefinition
├── ZoneId (string)
├── ZoneName (string)
├── Bounds
│   ├── MinX, MaxX, MinY, MaxY
├── SpawnPoints[]
│   ├── Id (string)
│   ├── X, Y (float)
│   ├── Type (SpawnPointType)
│   └── IsDefault (bool)
├── StaticEntities[]
│   ├── Id (int)
│   ├── Type (EntityType)
│   ├── X, Y (float)
│   └── Properties (Dictionary<string, object>)
└── MobSpawnPoints[]
    ├── Id (string)
    ├── X, Y (float)
    ├── MobType (string)
    ├── MaxCount (int)
    └── RespawnSeconds (int)
```

### Beispiel Zone-Definition

```json
{
  "zoneId": "startzone",
  "zoneName": "Startzone",
  "bounds": { "minX": 0, "maxX": 2048, "minY": 0, "maxY": 2048 },
  "spawnPoints": [
    { "id": "spawn-1", "x": 512, "y": 512, "type": "PlayerSpawn", "isDefault": true },
    { "id": "spawn-2", "x": 600, "y": 500, "type": "PlayerSpawn" }
  ],
  "staticEntities": [
    { 
      "id": 1001, 
      "type": "Door", 
      "x": 256, 
      "y": 384, 
      "properties": { "targetZone": "hauptstadt", "targetSpawn": "from-startzone" }
    },
    { 
      "id": 1002, 
      "type": "Portal", 
      "x": 1024, 
      "y": 1024, 
      "properties": { "targetZone": "wald", "targetSpawn": "portal-entry" }
    },
    { 
      "id": 1003, 
      "type": "Chest", 
      "x": 768, 
      "y": 256, 
      "properties": { "lootTable": "starter-chest" }
    },
    { 
      "id": 1004, 
      "type": "Sign", 
      "x": 500, 
      "y": 450, 
      "properties": { "text": "Willkommen in der Startzone!" }
    },
    { 
      "id": 1005, 
      "type": "NpcVendor", 
      "x": 300, 
      "y": 600, 
      "properties": { "vendorId": "starter-vendor" }
    }
  ],
  "mobSpawnPoints": [
    { "id": "mob-spawn-1", "x": 1200, "y": 800, "mobType": "Slime", "maxCount": 5, "respawnSeconds": 30 }
  ]
}
```

### Properties je Entity-Type

| EntityType | Properties | Beschreibung |
|------------|------------|--------------|
| **Door** | `targetZone`, `targetSpawn` | Zielzone und Spawnpoint beim Durchgehen |
| **Portal** | `targetZone`, `targetSpawn` | Teleport-Ziel |
| **Chest** | `lootTable`, `isOneTime` | Loot-Tabelle, einmalig plünderbar? |
| **Sign** | `text` | Anzeigetext |
| **NpcVendor** | `vendorId` | Referenz auf Vendor-Definition |
| **NpcQuestGiver** | `questIds` | Liste verfügbarer Quests |

### Datei-Ablage

```
2DMMO/
├── data/
│   └── zones/                          # Zone-Definitionen
│       ├── startzone.zone.json
│       ├── hauptstadt.zone.json
│       └── wald.zone.json
│
├── shared/
│   └── Mmo.Shared/
│       └── Zones/                      # Shared DTOs
│           ├── ZoneDefinition.cs
│           ├── SpawnPointDefinition.cs
│           ├── StaticEntityDefinition.cs
│           ├── MobSpawnPointDefinition.cs
│           └── ZoneDefinitionLoader.cs
```

### Laden der Zone-Definition

**Server:**
```csharp
var zone = ZoneDefinitionLoader.LoadFromFile("data/zones/startzone.zone.json");
```

**Client (Godot):**
```csharp
var json = FileAccess.GetFileAsString("res://data/zones/startzone.zone.json");
var zone = ZoneDefinitionLoader.LoadFromJson(json);
```
```

author: zeroknight
body:
Typically, when attempting to stop a container via `docker stop` or `podman stop`, the container engine will send a stop signal (SIGTERM by default) to the container's main process. There are two common ways this can go wrong:

1. The main process is run as PID 1 and doesn't register a signal handler for the stop signal and is consequently ignored
2. The main process is a shell script running a foreground process with no `trap`s and is consequently ignored by the *shell*

In either case, because the graceful stop signal is ignored, the container engine will then send a `SIGKILL` to the container process after a default timeout of 10 seconds. This is why some containers can be observed to "hang" when being stopped when they have no other reason to do so. Unlike `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT`, `SIGKILL` is an immediate, ungraceful stop that doesn't give the process time to clean up.

There is a fair bit of nuance in how `sh` and `bash` handle signals in different circumstances. The behavior relevant to the second case above and Dawarich's entrypoints in particular is that the shell ignores signals like `SIGTERM` and `SIGINT` when waiting on a foreground job; in this case, that would be: `bundle exec ${@}`. The reason that `SIGINT` is not ignored after pressing `Ctrl+C` while running the docker compose stack is because in that case the shell is **interactive** and the shell *does* respond to `SIGINT` then (c.f. the aforementioned nuance).

Thankfully, the fix is simple: `exec` the main process, which causes the server process to *replace* the shell process and directly receive any signals sent. Additionally, the stop signal for the app process should be set to `SIGINT`, as that is the expected signal for graceful shutdown. Sidekiq is fine with either `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT`, which is convenient.

## Bottom Line

Running the server as a foreground process in a shell script means the server process doesn't receive signals, which consequently means that the container cannot be cleanly stopped by signals. Importantly, means that `docker stop`, `podman stop`, or `systemctl stop` (Podman Quadlets) cannot cleanly stop the container; it will always be `SIGKILL`ed after a 10 second timeout.

Replacing the shell process with the server process via `exec ...` allows the server process to directly receive signals. Setting `STOPSIGNAL` to `SIGINT` in the Dockerfile means that the container engine will send the interrupt signal (same as pressing `Ctrl+C`) to the process, which is what puma is expecting.

author: ericsciple
body:
## Summary

Fixes false "Context access might be invalid" warnings for `secrets` and `vars` contexts.

Fixes:
- https://github.com/github/vscode-github-actions/issues/222
- https://github.com/actions/languageservices/issues/60
- https://github.com/actions/languageservices/issues/239

## Problem

When the list of valid secrets/vars cannot be determined, all `secrets.X` and `vars.X` accesses were flagged as potentially invalid. This happens when:
- The GitHub client is not yet initialized (during extension startup)
- The user is not authenticated to GitHub
- The repository context is unavailable
- No `contextProviderConfig` is provided (e.g., github-ui uses languageservice directly without fetching remote data)

## Solution

Mark `secrets` and `vars` contexts as "incomplete" when we don't have the full list of valid keys. This uses the existing `DescriptionDictionary.complete` property (already used for `workflow_call` secrets and dynamic environments) to tell the validator to skip validation rather than warn about unknown keys.

## Changes

1. **languageserver** - When GitHub client/repo unavailable, return incomplete context for secrets/vars
2. **languageservice** - When no contextProviderConfig provided, mark secrets/vars as incomplete

This covers both VS Code extension (uses languageserver) and github-ui (uses languageservice directly).

## Testing

All tests pass with 14 new tests added.

Add new weight mode where flip probability uses w = q^h + q^(2S-h) instead of
standard q or 1/q. S is a tunable integer parameter (default 10), h is the
height of horizontal (type-0) lozenges.

Changes across all implementations:
- 2025-11-28-ultimate-lozenge.cpp: main WASM with exported functions
- 2025-11-28-ultimate-lozenge-threaded.cpp: threaded WASM version
- lozenge_compute.wgsl: GPU Glauber dynamics shader
- cftp_compute.wgsl: GPU CFTP shader
- webgpu-lozenge-engine.js: WebGPU engine uniform buffer handling
- 2025-11-28-ultimate-lozenge.md: UI controls and dashed line at h=S

Acceptance probability: probUp = w/(1+w), probDown = 1/(1+w) where w = q^h + q^(2S-h)

**Backend data format support and normalization:**

* Refactored the `DashboardData` type in `page.tsx` to support both the new backend format (with grouped fields like `totais`, `faturamento`, `planos`, etc.) and legacy fields, allowing for flexible data handling and backward compatibility.

Manus-B: Ledger & Attestation Runtime Engineer

Implements core ledger runtime improvements:

1. Replay Verification System (backend/ledger/replay/)
   - Deterministic root recomputation from canonical payloads
   - Integrity verification with detailed diagnostics
   - Block and chain replay orchestration
   - Enforces invariant: replaying historical blocks MUST produce identical H_t

2. Epoch Root System (backend/ledger/epoch/)
   - Epoch-level aggregation of block attestation roots
   - E_t = MerkleRoot([H_0, H_1, ..., H_99]) for 100-block epochs
   - Efficient verification of large ledger segments

author: braden-w
body:
When the Button component was updated to support tooltips via the `tooltip` prop, the prop spread order caused user-provided event handlers to be overwritten.

The issue was that `tooltipProps` (from bits-ui's Tooltip.Trigger child snippet) was spread after `restProps`. In Svelte 5, later prop spreads override earlier ones, so any `onclick` handler passed to the Button would be replaced by the tooltip's internal handlers.

The fix swaps the spread order so user props take precedence:

```svelte
{...tooltipProps}
{...restProps}
```

The tooltip continues to work correctly because its ARIA attributes and hover/focus handlers that users don't typically override are still applied.

author: jerrysxie
body:
This pull request refactors how async UART wakers are managed in `src/uart.rs`. Instead of using a global array indexed by UART number, each UART instance now directly holds a reference to its own static `AtomicWaker`. This improves code clarity, safety, and encapsulation. Additionally, error handling for DMA channel access is improved by replacing `unwrap()` with a proper error return.

**Waker management improvements:**

* Replaced the global `UART_WAKERS` array with per-instance static `AtomicWaker`s, and updated all waker registration and wake calls to use the new approach. (`Info` now holds a `waker` reference rather than an index.) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2bd60f29989e7f927a4f3f4325d2ec2254df11c50d040d772fbeb67ce3abf008L1094-R1095) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2bd60f29989e7f927a4f3f4325d2ec2254df11c50d040d772fbeb67ce3abf008L1104-L1117) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2bd60f29989e7f927a4f3f4325d2ec2254df11c50d040d772fbeb67ce3abf008L1141-R1138) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-2bd60f29989e7f927a4f3f4325d2ec2254df11c50d040d772fbeb67ce3abf008L1160-R1163)
* Updated all uses of `UART_WAKERS[self.info.index]` to `self.info.waker`, ensuring each UART instance manages its own waker. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2bd60f29989e7f927a4f3f4325d2ec2254df11c50d040d772fbeb67ce3abf008L580-R581) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2bd60f29989e7f927a4f3f4325d2ec2254df11c50d040d772fbeb67ce3abf008L656-R657) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2bd60f29989e7f927a4f3f4325d2ec2254df11c50d040d772fbeb67ce3abf008L711-R712)

**Error handling improvements:**

* Replaced `.unwrap()` on DMA channel access with `.ok_or_else(|| Error::Fail)?` to return an error if the DMA channel is missing, improving robustness. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2bd60f29989e7f927a4f3f4325d2ec2254df11c50d040d772fbeb67ce3abf008L571-R572) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2bd60f29989e7f927a4f3f4325d2ec2254df11c50d040d772fbeb67ce3abf008L697-R698)

author: copilot
body:
Implements foundational terminal UI components for visual simulation interaction, replacing text-only CLI with rich dashboard experience.

## Components

- **Status Bar**: Global metrics (stability gauge, tick counter, alerts) with color-coded thresholds
- **City Map**: ASCII district grid with focus indicators (● ◐ ○) and selection support
- **Event Feed**: Chronological event stream with severity icons (🔴🟡🟢📖⚡) and priority classification
- **Context Panel**: Entity details (district/agent/faction) with modifier bars, resources, and shortage warnings
- **Command Bar**: Action buttons with keyboard shortcuts (Next/Run/Focus/Save/Why/Menu)
- **Layout Manager**: Screen composition system with UIState for view coordination

## Architecture

```python
from gengine.echoes.cli.components import render_status_bar, render_city_map
from gengine.echoes.cli.layout import UIState

# Compose UI from components
ui_state = UIState(current_view="map", selected_district="industrial-tier")
status = render_status_bar(game_state, alerts=["shortage"])
city_map = render_city_map(districts, ui_state)
```

All components use Rich library for terminal rendering. UIState manages view coordination and entity selection. Components designed for Live display integration (real-time updates during batch operations).

## Context-Aware Logic

- Event severity: Critical (crisis, level-3 shortages) → Economy (prices, shortages) → Warning → Info
- Modifier colors: Positive modifiers (prosperity, security) use inverted scale (high=green), negative modifiers (unrest, pollution) use standard scale (high=red)
- Resource thresholds: `SHORTAGE_THRESHOLD = 0.5` extracted as constant

## Test Coverage

30 tests covering component rendering, severity classification, color mapping, layout composition, and selection state. Zero security vulnerabilities (CodeQL).

## Integration Path

Next phase wires components into existing EchoesShell, adds Live display for batch tick updates, and implements view switching (agent roster, faction overview, timeline).

author: copilot
body:
Adds machine learning to BeaconStrategy, EntropyStrategy, and ExfilStrategy using Isolation Forest, KMeans clustering, and Local Outlier Factor respectively. ML runs automatically with 50+ samples, falls back to rule-based detection otherwise.

## Implementation

**ML Infrastructure**
- Feature scaling via StandardScaler
- Percentile-based score normalization (0-100) for analyst interpretability
- Helper functions for confidence levels (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) and feature importance

**Enhanced Strategies**
- **BeaconStrategy**: Isolation Forest on timing features (coeff_variation, mean_delta, connection_count) detects anomalous C2 patterns
- **EntropyStrategy**: KMeans (3-5 clusters) on entropy+length groups similar DGA domains by malware family
- **ExfilStrategy**: LOF on log-scaled traffic features identifies unusual upload/download outliers

**Output Columns** (added to each strategy)
```python
result_df['ml_anomaly_score']  # 0-100 percentile rank
result_df['ml_confidence']      # HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/NORMAL
result_df['ml_explanation']     # "🔴 ML HIGH CONFIDENCE: This beaconing pattern..."
```

## Testing

119 tests passing (114 existing + 5 new ML tests covering activation, fallback, and explanation validation)

## Documentation

- **ML_IMPLEMENTATION.md** (16KB): Algorithms, hyperparameters, feature engineering, usage patterns
- **ML_SUMMARY.md** (7KB): Quick reference with examples
- Column explanations updated with 🤖 indicators

## Example Output

```python
# Before: Rule-based only
beacon_score: 85

# After: Hybrid ML + rules
beacon_score: 85
ml_anomaly_score: 91.2
ml_confidence: HIGH
ml_explanation: "🔴 ML HIGH CONFIDENCE: Timing consistency and connection 
                 frequency are outliers. Key factors: High timing_consistency..."
```

**Design notes**: Percentile ranking over min-max scaling prioritizes interpretability and ranking preservation. No model persistence - trains fresh per query for simplicity and data freshness.

You are a senior ML engineer and software developer working on CampbellTrevor/221B - 221B Interactive Threat Hunting Dashboard, a Jupyter notebook-based threat hunting platform for security analysts.

PROJECT CONTEXT:
221B is a no-code threat hunting tool that connects to IONIC data stores via `ionic_scripting_framework` and provides a widget-based interface using ipywidgets. The dashboard uses Plotly for visualizations. UI logic lives in app.py, strategy logic in strategies.py. The tool is used by analysts of varying experience levels, including juniors.

CRITICAL PROJECT GOAL - ML IMPLEMENTATION:
Implement machine learning solutions for as many existing strategies as possible. Each ML-enhanced strategy should follow the complete ML lifecycle while remaining accessible to non-technical analysts.

ML IMPLEMENTATION LIFECYCLE (for each strategy):
1. MODEL SELECTION: Choose an appropriate ML model for the detection task (e.g., Isolation Forest for anomaly detection, clustering for pattern discovery, classification for known threat types)
2. FEATURE IDENTIFICATION: Identify which data attributes are relevant for the model
3. FEATURE ENGINEERING: Transform raw data into meaningful features the model can use
4. HYPERPARAMETER TUNING: Configure model parameters appropriately (can use sensible defaults with optional tuning)
5. TRAIN/TEST SPLIT: Validate model performance before applying to real data
6. MODEL APPLICATION: Use the trained model to score/classify the analyst's data

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR ML FEATURES:
- ZERO CODE: Analysts should not need to write any code - ML happens behind the scenes
- EXPLAINABILITY: Junior analysts need to understand results. For every ML output:
  * Explain what the model is doing in plain English
  * Show why a record was flagged (feature contributions, scores, etc.)
  * Provide confidence levels or probability scores where applicable
  * Include tooltips or help text explaining ML concepts
- TRANSPARENCY: Show the analyst what features were used and how the model made decisions
- GRACEFUL FALLBACK: If ML fails or insufficient data, fall back to rule-based detection

IMPORTANT ML CONSIDERATIONS:
- UNLABELED DATA: All data is unlabeled - use unsupervised learning (Isolation Forest, clustering, autoencoders) or semi-supervised approaches like PU Learning (Positive-Unlabeled) where appropriate
- TRAIN ON QUERY: Models train fresh on each query dataset - no pre-trained models across strategies
- MODEL CACHING: Cache trained models for reuse, but invalidate cache when the dataset/table changes
- SMALL DATASETS: Handle gracefully - require minimum sample sizes (e.g., 50+ rows) before applying ML, otherwise use rule-based fallback
- IMBALANCED DATA: Threat data is inherently imbalanced (few anomalies, many normal). Use techniques suited for this: Isolation Forest, LOF, or density-based approaches that don't require balanced classes
- SPEED: Keep ML fast enough for interactive use - avoid algorithms that scale poorly with data size
- FEATURE SCALING: Always scale/normalize features before applying distance-based or gradient-based algorithms

UI/UX FOR ML:
- Add clear explanations of what ML is happening behind the scenes
- Show model performance metrics in an understandable way
- Visualize feature importance and decision factors
- Use color coding and visual cues to highlight ML-driven insights
- Consider an "Explain This Result" option for flagged items

RECOMMENDED LIBRARIES (already available or commonly installed):
- scikit-learn: Isolation Forest, Random Forest, KMeans, StandardScaler, train_test_split
- scipy: statistical functions already in use
- pandas/numpy: data manipulation
- Plotly: visualization of ML results

Guidelines:
- Implement ML in strategies.py within the existing strategy classes
- UI updates in app.py to display ML explanations and results
- Maintain the no-code philosophy throughout
- Start with strategies most amenable to ML (anomaly detection strategies like Beacon, Entropy)
- Use unsupervised methods where labeled data isn't available
- Document the ML approach in code comments

FILE STRUCTURE - IMPORTANT:

- Do NOT create excessive new files

DO NOT:

body:
Extended inference pipeline to process receipts, invoices, bills, and financial documents with automatic document type classification. All extracted fields now include confidence scores. Added support for three new commercially-licensed vision-language models and removed non-commercially licensed models to ensure all models are suitable for commercial use.

## Changes

### C# Data Models
- **`InferenceResult.cs`**: Added 24 document-specific fields
  - Document classification: `DocumentType`
  - Invoice: `InvoiceNumber`, `DueDate`, `PaymentTerms`, `CustomerName`, `CustomerAddress`, `PoNumber`
  - Bill: `AccountNumber`, `BillingPeriod`, `PreviousBalance`, `CurrentCharges`, `AmountDue`
  - Receipt: `PaymentMethod`, `CashierName`, `RegisterNumber`
  - General: `Discount`, `Shipping`, `Notes`

### Python Inference Layer
- **`field_extractor.py`**: Added `classify_document_type()` using keyword-based heuristics; 15 new extraction methods for document-specific fields
- **`receipt_processor.py`**: Extended result structure to support all document types; maintains backward compatibility
- **`idefics2.py`**: Enhanced prompt template for multi-document classification; added field parsing for invoice/bill fields
- **`donut.py`**: Document type hardcoded to "receipt" (CORD-v2 is receipt-specific)

### New Vision-Language Models
Added three new model implementations for enhanced document processing:

- **`phi3_vision.py`**: Microsoft Phi-3-Vision (MIT license) - Lightweight and efficient with 128k context window (~7GB memory)
- **`internvl.py`**: OpenGVLab InternVL (MIT license) - High accuracy with strong OCR capabilities (2-8GB memory, multiple variants)
- **`qwen2_vl.py`**: Alibaba Qwen2-VL (Apache 2.0 license) - Efficient architecture with strong performance (4-7GB memory)
- **`__init__.py`**: Updated model factory with automatic selection logic for all models

All models support multi-document processing with automatic classification and confidence-scored field extraction.

### Removed Non-Commercial Models
- **Removed `layoutlmv3.py`**: Eliminated LayoutLMv3 model implementation (non-commercial license)
- **Removed `fine_tuning.md`**: Removed LayoutLMv3-specific documentation
- **Updated all references**: Removed all LayoutLMv3 references from code, documentation, tests, and configuration files

### Example Output

```json
{
  "document_type": {"value": "invoice", "confidence": 0.88},
  "vendor_name": {"value": "ACME Corp", "confidence": 0.95},
  "invoice_number": {"value": "INV-2024-001", "confidence": 0.87},
  "due_date": {"value": "2024-02-15", "confidence": 0.85},
  "customer_name": {"value": "Client LLC", "confidence": 0.86},
  "total_amount": {"value": "1250.00", "confidence": 0.96},
  "line_items": [...]
}
```

## Model Capabilities

All models have commercial-friendly licenses (MIT or Apache 2.0):

| Model | Receipts | Invoices | Bills | License | Notes |
|-------|----------|----------|-------|---------|-------|
| Donut (CORD-v2) | Optimized | Limited | Limited | MIT | Receipt-specific fine-tuning |
| IDEFICS2 | Excellent | Excellent | Excellent | Apache 2.0 | Multi-document support |
| Phi-3-Vision | Excellent | Excellent | Excellent | MIT | Efficient, 128k context |
| InternVL | Excellent | Excellent | Excellent | MIT | Strong OCR capabilities |
| Qwen2-VL | Excellent | Excellent | Excellent | Apache 2.0 | Balanced performance |

## Documentation
- Created `Ocr/docs/supported_documents.md` with field mappings by document type and comprehensive model recommendations
- Updated main README.md with expanded model list in technology stack
- Updated Ocr/README.md with complete model comparison table and capabilities
- Updated CLI version command to list all commercially-licensed models
- All documentation updated to reflect only commercially-licensed models

## Commercial Licensing
All remaining models use MIT or Apache 2.0 licenses, which are fully commercial-friendly open source licenses suitable for commercial use without restrictions.

## Notes
- **PaddlePaddle**: Already integrated as OCR engine (not an inference model)
- **omni-embed-nemotron-3b**: Embedding model, not suitable for document field extraction
- **NVIDIA-Nemotron models**: Not added as current model set comprehensively covers all use cases
- **LayoutLMv3**: Removed due to licensing concerns - all remaining models are commercially licensed

This PR refactors `GenericCardSystem` to use the **Handler/Command Pattern** (Level 1 of the proposed refactoring plan). It replaces the monolithic `switch` statements with a registry of `IActionHandler` implementations.

Key Changes:
*   **Architecture**: Introduced `IActionHandler` interface and `EffectSystem` registry.
*   **Refactoring**: Moved action logic (DRAW, TAP, DESTROY, SEARCH, etc.) into individual handler classes under `src/engine/card_system/handlers/`.

Previously, some actions incorrectly used `active_player_id` as the controller, causing issues with Shield Triggers (effects triggering on the opponent's turn). The fix correctly derives the controller from the `source_instance_id` across all zones (including `effect_buffer`).
*   **Testing**: Verified with `python/tests/test_atomic_actions.py` and `python/tests/test_engine_basics.py`. Added temporary regression test `test_shield_trigger_controller.py` during development (now removed).

This change improves maintainability by adhering to the Open/Closed Principle for new action types and fixes a logic error in effect resolution.

author: aj47
body:
## Summary

Fixes #424 - Profile text truncated after save - only first line retained

## Problem

When a user:
1. Created a new profile using "Save as New"
2. Edited the profile text (guidelines) in the textarea
3. Clicked "Save Changes"
4. Switched to a different profile
5. Switched back to the newly created profile

The text was truncated - only the original content was displayed, not the edited content.

## Root Cause

When the user clicked "Save Changes", the `saveAdditionalGuidelines()` function only saved the guidelines to `mcpToolsSystemPrompt` in the config. However, it did **not** update the current profile's `guidelines` field in the profile service.

When switching back to the profile, `setCurrentProfile` loaded the profile's stored `guidelines` (which was stale - containing only the original content from profile creation) and wrote it to `mcpToolsSystemPrompt`, overwriting the user's changes.

## Solution

Modified the `saveAdditionalGuidelines()` function in `settings-tools.tsx` to:
1. Save the guidelines to the config (existing behavior)
2. **Also update the current profile's guidelines** if it's a non-default profile

This ensures the profile stays in sync with what the user saves in the textarea.

## Changes

- Added `currentProfileQuery` to fetch the current profile
- Added `updateProfileMutation` to update profile guidelines
- Modified `saveAdditionalGuidelines()` to also update the profile when saving

- ✅ TypeScript compilation passes
- ✅ All 32 tests pass

### High-Level Summary
This PR integrates the LabTOP model (Hur et al., 2024) into a reproducible PyTorch pipeline for lab test outcome prediction from ICU EHR data. The integration adds:

- Digit-level lab value tokenization

- Computes predictions for next lab value events

**Example script:**

On-top of #59950

Alternative to https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/pull/60338

---

GlobalISel is LLVM's modern instruction selector that is designed to replace
both FastISel and SelectionDAG. On AArch64, it is mature and enabled by default
at -O0 in upstream LLVM.

This enables GlobalISel with fallback mode on AArch64, which provides faster
instruction selection than SelectionDAG while maintaining correctness by
falling back to SelectionDAG for unsupported patterns.

Note: This requires RemoveJuliaAddrspacesPass to run before codegen, which is
already the case in the current pipeline (see pipeline.cpp comment about
GlobalISel not liking Julia's address spaces).

author: gurmeetsaran
body:
## Summary
Add comprehensive support for the modern Python 3.10+ pipe-none syntax (`X | None`) alongside the traditional `Optional[X]` syntax in Pydantic model definitions.

## Problem
The `X | None` syntax (PEP 604) was not recognized because it creates a `types.UnionType` without the `__origin__` attribute that `Optional[X]` has. This caused Optional handling to be skipped entirely when using the modern syntax.

## Solution
- Created `is_union_type()` helper function that properly detects both union syntaxes using `get_origin()`
- Updated all adapter files to use the new helper (11 occurrences across 5 adapters)
- Both syntaxes now work identically in all contexts

## Changes

### Core Fix
- **_types.py**: Added `is_union_type()` helper function
- Updated `is_struct_type()`, `unwrap_optional_type()` to use new helper

### Adapter Updates
- **DuckDB**: 3 locations fixed
- **BigQuery**: 3 locations fixed
- **Presto/Athena/Trino**: 3 locations fixed
- **Snowflake**: 1 location fixed
- **Redshift**: 1 location fixed

## Testing

### Unit Tests (7 tests)
- `tests/test_union_syntax_support.py`
- Tests for `is_union_type()`, `unwrap_optional_type()`, `is_struct_type()`
- Validates both `Optional[X]` and `X | None` syntax

### Integration Tests (14 tests)
- `tests/integration/test_union_syntax_integration.py`
- Tests all database adapters (DuckDB, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Athena, Trino)
- Both CTE mode and physical tables mode
- 10 pass locally, 4 require external DB connections

## Example Usage

Both syntaxes now work identically:

```python
from typing import Optional
from pydantic import BaseModel
from decimal import Decimal

# Traditional syntax - still works
class UserOld(BaseModel):
    name: str
    email: Optional[str] = None
    balance: Optional[Decimal] = None

# Modern syntax - now works!  
class UserNew(BaseModel):
    name: str
    email: str | None = None
    balance: Decimal | None = None
```

## Test Results
```
✅ 7 unit tests pass
✅ 10 integration tests pass
⏭️ 4 integration tests require external DB (Redshift, Trino)
✅ 72 existing type-related tests still pass
✅ Type checking passes
```

author: toakleaf
body:
When a property accessor ($property) was used inside a nested rule to access a merged property (property+:), the parent selector's transform would incorrectly contain duplicate values.

The issue was that Property.Eval() was using the original Declaration pointers when merging properties. When mergeRules() modified the first declaration's Value, it modified the original in the parent ruleset. Later, ToCSSVisitor.mergeRules() would merge again, causing duplication.

The fix creates copies of Declaration objects before calling mergeRules, matching the Less.js behavior (see property.js lines 32-44). This ensures the original declarations in the parent ruleset are never modified.

Example:
.accessor-merged {
  transform+: rotate(45deg);
  transform+: scale(1.5);
  .result {
    animation-transform: $transform;
  }
}

Before fix (incorrect):
.accessor-merged { transform: rotate(45deg), scale(1.5), scale(1.5); }

After fix (correct):
.accessor-merged { transform: rotate(45deg), scale(1.5); }

## Summary
Add org-level reusable workflow for FIPS 140-2/140-3 compliance checking in Python projects, converted from the homelab-infra repository workflow.

## Changes

### New Features
- **Reusable FIPS Workflow**: Centralized workflow for FIPS compliance checking across all Python repositories
- **Configurable Inputs**: 7 customizable parameters (strict mode, test inclusion, Python version, etc.)
- **PR Integration**: Automatic comments with compliance summaries and fix hints
- **Runtime Testing**: Optional simulated FIPS environment testing
- **Comprehensive Documentation**: Complete usage guide with examples and troubleshooting

### Files Added
- `.github/workflows/python-fips-compatibility.yml` - Reusable workflow definition
- `workflow-templates/python-fips-compatibility.yml` - Template for downstream repos
- `workflow-templates/python-fips-compatibility.properties.json` - GitHub template metadata
- `docs/workflows/python-fips-compatibility.md` - Complete documentation

### Bug Fixes
- **python-reuse.yml**: Updated `fsfe/reuse-action` from v4.0.0 (invalid commit hash) to v6.0.0 (latest stable)

## Usage Example

Downstream repositories can now use:

```yaml
name: FIPS Compatibility

on:
  pull_request:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 10 * * 1'

jobs:
  fips-check:
    uses: ByronWilliamsCPA/.github/.github/workflows/python-fips-compatibility.yml@main
    with:
      strict-mode: false
      include-tests: true
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
```

## Benefits
- ✅ Centralized FIPS compliance checking across org
- ✅ Reduces workflow duplication in individual repositories
- ✅ Easy to maintain and update in one location
- ✅ Consistent FIPS validation standards
- ✅ Comprehensive documentation for adoption

author: bplatz
body:
### Summary
Adds support for AWS S3 Express One Zone storage, providing single-digit millisecond latency (~1-5ms vs ~100-200ms for standard S3). Uses a hybrid approach: AWS SDK v2 for session management only, while continuing to use manual HTTP signing for data operations to avoid GraalVM compatibility issues.
### Key Features
Automatic bucket detection - Express One Zone buckets are auto-detected by the --x-s3 suffix
Session credential management - CreateSession API calls with 5-minute credential caching
Lambda IAM role support - Handles temporary credentials (access key, secret key, and session token)
Split storage ready - Use Express for indexes (hot data) and standard S3 for commits (archival)
GraalVM compatible - Successfully compiles to native image with AWS SDK v2
### Changes
**New Files**
src/fluree/db/storage/s3_express.clj - Session credential management using AWS SDK v2
**Modified Files**
src/fluree/db/storage/s3.clj - Auto-detect Express buckets, handle session credentials, virtual-hosted URL construction
docs/S3_STORAGE_GUIDE.md - Configuration examples, troubleshooting, clarified that s3Endpoint is optional
deps.edn - Added software.amazon.awssdk/s3 dependency
solo3 (serverless) Changes
src/fluree/serverless/lambda/common.clj - Split storage configuration with no explicit endpoints
### Technical Details
Session Credential Flow
Base IAM credentials → CreateSession API → Temporary session credentials
Session credentials cached for 5 minutes (aligned with S3 Express session duration)
Automatic refresh 30 seconds before expiration
Session token sent via x-amz-s3session-token header (Express-specific)
### Lambda Support
Uses AwsSessionCredentials to support Lambda's temporary IAM role credentials
Extracts AWS_SESSION_TOKEN from environment and passes to CreateSession API
Previously only supported AwsBasicCredentials (access key + secret only)
### URL Construction
Express One Zone: https://bucket--use1-az1--x-s3.s3express-use1-az1.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/path
Standard S3: https://bucket.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/path
Uses service name s3express vs s3 for signature calculation
Configuration Example
```
{
  "@graph": [
    {
      "@id": "commitStorage",
      "@type": "Storage",
      "s3Bucket": "fluree-commits"
    },
    {
      "@id": "indexStorage",
      "@type": "Storage",
      "s3Bucket": "fluree-idx--use1-az1--x-s3"
    }
  ]
}
```
Note: No s3Endpoint needed - Fluree auto-detects from bucket name.

author: toakleaf
body:
When accessing a variable from a namespace and using it in a math operation (e.g., #typography[@base-size] * 1.25), the value was not being properly converted from Anonymous to Dimension, causing the math operation to remain unevaluated in the output.

The fix adds dimension string parsing (via TryParseDimensionString) to the generic evaluator path in NamespaceValue.Eval, ensuring that values like "16px" are properly converted to Dimension nodes before being used in math operations.

This matches the existing behavior in the Declaration-specific path but was missing for the generic Value evaluator path which is used when accessing namespace variables.

author: volkamalak
body:
This commit resolves all theme-related UI bugs, including the invisible Toolbar text and icons, by implementing a consistent and correctly defined color and theme structure.

- **Root Cause:** The Toolbar was not visible because the application theme was missing primary color definitions, and the `AppBarLayout` in the layout file was overriding the main theme with an outdated, dark theme.
- **Solution:**
    1.  A new, clear color palette was defined in `colors.xml`, including a white `colorPrimary` for the Toolbar and black `textColorPrimary` for text/icons to ensure visibility.
    2.  The base application theme in `themes.xml` was updated to correctly reference these new colors.
    3.  All hardcoded theme overrides were removed from the `AppBarLayout` and `Toolbar` in `activity_main.xml`, allowing them to properly inherit the corrected application theme.
- **Outcome:** The Toolbar and all its elements are now clearly visible, and the application has a consistent, professional theme that resolves all previous UI bugs and crashes.

author: tiann
body:
## Bug: First Message Not Sent to Agent on New Session Creation

### Symptoms
When creating a new session with prefilled text, the first message appears in the UI but the agent never responds. User must copy and resend the message manually.

When Claude starts the binary via spawn, it is more likely to be triggered because spawn is time-consuming.

### Root Cause
Race condition between app sending message and agent WebSocket connection.

### Why

  - Previously, the app sent the first message before the agent’s WebSocket connected; the broadcast was missed even though stored in DB. Now
    the first send is deferred until the agent is actually listening.

  Timeline Diagrams

  Before fix (message lost)
```
  App                              Server                      Agent
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  machineSpawnNewSession ────────► spawn daemon ─────────────► Agent starting…
  refreshSessions (session in DB)                                │ (connecting)
  sendMessage(input) ───────────► store in DB ✓                 │ not connected
                                │ broadcast via WebSocket ────► (no recipient)
  navigate to session                                               │
                                                                      ▼
                                                              Agent connects
                                                              SDK ready
                                                              (first message missed)
```

  After fix (message delivered)

```
  App                              Server                      Agent
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  machineSpawnNewSession ────────► spawn daemon ─────────────► Agent starting…
  refreshSessions (loads session)                                │ (connecting)
  sendMessage(input) ──┐                                          │
                       │ waitForSessionReady()                    │
                       │  - waits ready event / active            │
                       │  - 15s timeout fallback                  │
                       │                                          ▼
                       │                                    WebSocket connects
                       │                                    sends 'ready' event
                       └─ resumes ───────────────► broadcast message ─────────► receives message
  navigate to session
  Agent responds
```

## Changes
- Added reconnect_client() method to MinifluxTuiApp to recreate stale API connections
- Updated MinifluxClient to catch broader range of connection errors (OSError, BrokenPipeError)
- Added automatic reconnection with retry logic in refresh operations (_do_refresh, _do_refresh_all_feeds, _do_sync_entries)
- Updated tests to properly mock async reconnect_client() method

## Problem
After long idle periods (overnight), the HTTP connection becomes stale and refresh operations fail, requiring the application to be closed and reopened.

## Solution
- When a connection error occurs, attempt to reconnect automatically before retrying the operation
- Catch OSError and BrokenPipeError in addition to ConnectionError and TimeoutError
- Provide user feedback when reconnection is attempted
- Gracefully handle reconnection failures

## Related Issues
- Fixes issue where refresh errors out after overnight idle period

author: taylorleese
body:
## Summary

Add Dockerfile for deploying mcp-toolz to the Glama platform with full HTTP/SSE support via mcp-proxy.

## Key Changes

- **Add Dockerfile.glama** - Production-ready Docker configuration for Glama
  - Uses `mcp-proxy@5.12.0` to expose Python MCP server via HTTP/SSE endpoints
  - Defaults to `main` branch with ARG override for pinning to specific commits
  - Includes critical `--` separator fix for mcp-proxy argument parsing
  - Passes hadolint Docker linting with proper SHELL directive
  
- **Update .gitignore** - Remove Dockerfile.glama exclusion

## Critical Fix

The `--` separator in the CMD is essential:
```dockerfile
CMD ["mcp-proxy","/app/.venv/bin/python","--","-m","mcp_server"]
```

Without it, mcp-proxy's yargs parser interprets Python's `-m` flag as an mcp-proxy option, causing the server to fail to start. This was the root cause of the original Glama build failure.

## Testing

✅ Server starts successfully  
✅ Health check (`/ping`) returns "pong"  
✅ All pre-commit hooks pass  
✅ Tested with both default (main) and pinned commits

## Usage

**Default build (uses main branch):**
```bash
docker build -t mcp-toolz -f Dockerfile.glama .
```

**Production build (pinned to specific commit):**
```bash
docker build --build-arg GIT_REF=<commit-hash> -t mcp-toolz -f Dockerfile.glama .
```

author: matthew11012
body:
## 1. What does this PR do?

This PR introduces significant improvements to the curriculum feature, focusing on both the backend lesson generation process and the frontend user experience. It refines the AI prompts for generating lesson content to be more pedagogically sound, removes the 'READ' activity from lesson generation, and introduces a collapsible sidebar for the curriculum on desktop.

## 2. Why is this change important?

These changes aim to enhance the quality and consistency of the generated lesson content, making it more accessible and useful for learners. The UI improvements, such as the collapsible sidebar, provide a more flexible and user-friendly experience, allowing users to focus on the lesson content. The increased timeout for lesson generation also improves the robustness of the system.

## 3. Key Changes

### Backend (Curriculum Generation)

-   **Prompt Engineering:**
    -   The system prompt for `generateLessonFromOutline` has been extensively updated to enforce stricter pedagogical standards.
    -   Generated content now consistently includes **Pinyin** and **English glosses** for all Chinese text.
    -   The AI is now instructed to use **simplified Chinese only**.
    -   Specific formatting rules for tables and examples have been added to improve readability and avoid redundancy.
-   **Lesson Structure:**
    -   The 'READ' activity has been removed from the lesson generation flow.
    -   Quiz generation (`generateQuizItems`) now relies solely on 'GRAMMAR' content.
-   **API Robustness:**
    -   The timeout for `generateLesson` has been increased from 2 minutes to 5 minutes to handle more complex lesson generation tasks.

### Frontend (UI/UX)

-   **Collapsible Sidebar:**
    -   The curriculum navigation sidebar on desktop is now collapsible, allowing users to maximize their screen real estate.
-   **Rich Content Rendering:**
    -   The lesson viewer now uses a `MarkdownRenderer` for pitfalls (`bad`, `good`, `note`) and comprehension question prompts, allowing for richer formatting in these sections.
-   **UI Polish:**
    -   Minor padding and layout adjustments have been made to the lesson viewer and breadcrumb navigation for a cleaner look.

## 4. Implementation Details

<details>
<summary>Click to expand for implementation details</summary>

### File Changes

-   **`apps/backend/src/curriculum/curriculum.service.ts`**: Removed the 'READ' activity from the `generateAndGetLessonActivities` method.
-   **`apps/backend/src/openai/openai.service.ts`**: Updated the prompts for `generateQuizItems` and `generateLessonFromOutline` with new instructions.
-   **`apps/frontend/src/app/curriculum/[unit]/[lesson]/page.tsx`**: Implemented `MarkdownRenderer` for pitfalls and comprehension questions, and adjusted UI padding.
-   **`apps/frontend/src/components/curriculum/curriculum-navigation-sidebar.tsx`**: Added the collapsible sidebar functionality for desktop view.
-   **`apps/frontend/src/lib/api/curriculum.ts`**: Increased the timeout for the `generateLesson` API call.

</details>

## 5. How to Manually Test

1.  **Lesson Generation:**
    -   Generate a new lesson and verify that the content adheres to the new prompt standards (Pinyin, English glosses, simplified Chinese).
    -   Inspect the generated quizzes to ensure they are based only on the 'GRAMMAR' section.
2.  **Collapsible Sidebar:**
    -   On a desktop device, open the curriculum and test the new sidebar toggle button. Verify that the sidebar collapses and expands smoothly.
3.  **Rich Content Rendering:**
    -   View a lesson with pitfalls and comprehension questions. Confirm that any Markdown in these sections is rendered correctly.
4.  **UI/UX:**
    -   Check the lesson viewer for the updated padding and sticky breadcrumb navigation.

-   [ ] I have added a testing framework and written unit/integration/a11y tests.
-   [x] I have tested my changes on the relevant devices/browsers to ensure no regressions.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> Can you turn this into a new blog post and open a pull request make sure it looks good too! Remember title header is rendered in the post too so no need to have it in the body too
> 
> 
> Coding Agents Suck
> 
> (Until they suddenly don’t.)
> 
> If you hang around engineers long enough, you’ll hear some version of the title muttered under someone’s breath. Usually it comes from the senior folks who’ve lived through enough “revolutionary” tools to know they all end the same way: a rewrite, a migration, and a wiki page nobody updates. Fatigue is earned.
> 
> Still, let’s be honest—coding agents aren’t fading into the sunset. And I’ve got an unusual test case that convinced me: Advent of Code.
> 
> Last Year: Pushing a Boulder Uphill
> 
> Last year I made myself a promise: solve each Advent of Code problem manually, then call in AI only when properly stuck. I was using Cursor and a handful of their agents. The plan was simple—warm up on part one, wrestle with part two, and let AI shove me across the finish line when I needed a kick.
> 
> This was optimistic.
> 
> I ran head-first into three problems:
> 	1.	Context windows were tiny. I couldn’t fit the whole problem, my code, and input data. The model was basically guessing.
> 	2.	Generated code was a mess. Slow, unoptimized, and hard to debug.
> 	3.	Prompts had to be so compact they were borderline haiku.
> 
> If you’ve ever written code without really understanding the ticket, you know how this goes. You get code that technically “runs,” but you can’t trust it, can’t reason about it, and definitely can’t optimize it. That was me and the agent—two people squinting at a problem neither of us had the full picture of.
> 
> By December 6th, I tapped out. AI hadn’t helped me ship faster; it had just made my confusion multiline.
> 
> This Year: Everything Changed
> 
> Yes, yes, Advent of Code says “don’t use AI.”
> Are you my parent? No? Then I’m moving on.
> 
> This year I did something different. I wrote a first pass for days 1–3. If the code didn’t work—assuming the bug wasn’t something embarrassing like resetting a counter inside a loop—I dropped the full problem, sample input, and a short explanation into Claude Code.
> 
> And the experience was honestly jarring.
> 
> For the first time, I could hand it the entire problem: prompt, explanation, sample data—everything. The agent looked at my repo, figured out the language, picked the right file, walked through the reasoning, and produced runnable code.
> 
> It was about 50% correct on the first try.
> As in: run, submit, done.
> 
> That felt borderline illegal.
> 
> The other 50%? That was on me. Either I forced the model to work around my half-baked solution, or I didn’t give it enough context to do its job. If I wiped my code and said “solve it clean,” it usually did.
> 
> The Real Shift: Driver vs. Navigator
> 
> The surprising part wasn’t that AI wrote working code. It was that I understood the code. It was clean. Predictable. Idiomatic. And then I, human that I am, inevitably made it worse.
> 
> Trying to shoehorn AI’s solution into my half-finished version felt like when a kid asks you to help finish their LEGO set but refuses to let you undo the crooked pieces they placed earlier. The model will contort itself to preserve your mistakes.
> 
> And that’s when it clicked: AI isn’t the junior developer in this pairing session anymore.
> It’s closer to the person who just wants to finish the ticket and go home, but keeps getting slowed down because you won’t let them refactor the weird stuff you wrote at midnight.
> 
> The tool landscape changed while we weren’t looking. The “AI is just a toy” narrative already feels dated. Whatever you think of the hype cycle, coding agents are becoming another tool in the standard kit—and eventually, the question won’t be should you use them, but why aren’t you?
> 


</details>

author: gitrlawton
body:
**Current State**

Currently, collection folders in the sidebar show only their name and icon, with no indication of how many requests they contain. This makes it difficult to assess at a glance which collections are actively used, which are empty, or which might need reorganization.

**Proposed Feature (Solution)**

With this PR, each collection folder in the sidebar displays a small badge showing the total number of requests it contains (including requests nested inside tags/folders). The badge appears to the right of the collection name, updates dynamically when requests are added or removed, and is hidden for empty collections to reduce visual clutter.

Changes made:

1. Added **RequestSidebarItem.vue** computed property - Created `collectionRequestCount` (lines 205-213) to calculate the total number of requests in a collection by accessing `collections[uid].requests.length`, which includes all requests regardless of nesting in tags.

2. Modified **RequestSidebarItem.vue** template structure - Wrapped the collection title in a flex container (line 513) with `gap-1` and `overflow-hidden` to accommodate the badge alongside the title while preventing layout overflow.

3. Added **RequestSidebarItem.vue** badge element - Inserted a conditional badge `<span>` (lines 517-521) that renders when `collectionRequestCount > 0`, styled with Tailwind classes `bg-b-2 text-c-3 inline-flex min-w-5 shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-full px-1.5 py-0.5 text-[10px] font-medium` for consistent design system integration and proper badge appearance.

**Related Issue**

Fixes Issue #24  (called Issue # 16 - [FEATURE] Add Request Count Badge to Collection Folders in Sidebar ...)

author: copilot
body:
The Streamlit app was incomplete (54 lines, single function stub) with frequent AttributeErrors and no resilient data fetching. Built production-ready portfolio analytics application with three-tier fallback mechanism.

## Core Implementation

- **`load_weights()`**: Case-insensitive CSV parsing, automatic weight normalization per wave, `@st.cache_data` decorator (5min TTL)
- **`fetch_price_history()`**: Yahoo Finance → local `prices.csv` → synthetic data generation. Silent fallback on API restrictions
- **`compute_portfolio_engine()`**: Date-aligned price series, weighted returns, cumulative NAV tracking for wave and benchmark
- **Streamlit UI**: Sidebar navigation, metrics dashboard (4 KPIs), holdings table, performance charts

## Data Flow

```python
@dataclass
class WaveEngineResult:
    wave_return: float
    benchmark_return: float
    exposure: float
    smartsafe_allocation: float
    holdings: pd.DataFrame
    nav_series: Optional[pd.Series]
    benchmark_nav_series: Optional[pd.Series]

# Three-tier fallback
def fetch_price_history(ticker: str, days: int = 365) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = fetch_yahoo_price_history(ticker, days)
    if df is not None: return df
    
    df = load_prices_from_csv(ticker)
    if df is not None: return df
    
    return generate_synthetic_prices(ticker, days)
```

## Configuration Constants

```python
LIVE_MODE_EXPOSURE = 1.0  # 100% exposure
DEMO_MODE_EXPOSURE = 0.5  # 50% exposure
DEFAULT_EXCHANGE = "NASDAQ"

WAVE_BENCHMARKS = {
    "AI_Wave": "QQQ",
    "Growth_Wave": "SPY",
    # ...
}
```

## Error Handling

- Missing CSV: Clear error messages, empty dataframes
- Invalid columns: Case-insensitive matching with fallback
- Network failures: Automatic fallback to local/synthetic data
- Missing tickers: Continue with available data

## UI Components

- Holdings table using native `st.dataframe()` (avoids tabulate dependency)
- Google Finance quick links for top 5 holdings
- Performance chart comparing wave vs benchmark NAV
- Responsive layout with proper state management

## Screenshots

**AI_Wave Dashboard**

**Growth_Wave Dashboard**

## Files Changed

- `app.py`: 54 → 596 lines (complete implementation)
- `README.md`: 2 → 266 lines (comprehensive documentation)
- `.gitignore`: Fixed corrupted file with proper Python exclusions

body:
## Description

Evaluates the proposed `inherit()` function for class inheritance in AlaSQL through comprehensive performance testing.

## Changes

Created test suite in `test/performance/class/#117/`:

- **perf-inheritance-patterns.js** - Benchmarks 4 inheritance patterns (current, proposed, ES6, simple)
- **perf-object-creation.js** - Object instantiation with varying complexity (5-10 properties)
- **perf-method-calls.js** - Method invocation across inheritance chains
- **perf-multi-level-issue.js** - Demonstrates stack overflow in multi-level inheritance
- **run-all-tests.js** - Test runner with consolidated results
- **README.md** - Documentation

## Key Findings

### Performance
Current pattern outperforms proposed by 24-28% across all metrics:
- Object creation: 8-67% faster (complexity-dependent)
- Method calls: 61% faster average

### Critical Bug
Proposed pattern fails with multi-level inheritance:

```js
function inherit(child, parent) {
    child.prototype = Object.create(parent.prototype);
    child.prototype.constructor = child;
    child.prototype.super = function () {
        parent.apply(this, arguments);  // Problem: gets overwritten
    };
}

// GrandParent → Parent → Child
inherit(Parent, GrandParent);
inherit(Child, Parent);  // Overwrites Parent.prototype.super
new Child();  // Stack overflow: Parent.super now calls Parent, not GrandParent
```

### Recommendation
Keep current pattern (`Parent.call(this, args)`). Safer, faster, works at any depth.

## Testing

```bash
node test/performance/class/#117/run-all-tests.js
```

author: copilot
body:
The workflow was failing with `xvfb-run: error: Xvfb failed to start` after rendering multiple OpenSCAD files. Each `xvfb-run` invocation attempted to spawn a new Xvfb instance, eventually exhausting display resources.

## Changes

### Xvfb Fix
- **Start persistent Xvfb instance**: Launch Xvfb once on display `:99` with robust startup verification using `xdpyinfo` (from x11-utils package)
- **Remove xvfb-run wrappers**: Replace all `xvfb-run openscad` commands with direct `openscad` invocations using `DISPLAY=:99`
- **Add cleanup**: Terminate Xvfb gracefully (SIGTERM) with SIGKILL fallback, runs always even on failure

### Workflow Separation
- **Split workflows**: Created two independent workflow files for better organization and parallel execution:
  - `openscad-render.yml` - Generates visual outputs (PNG renders, animations, CNC files)
  - `openscad-structural-analysis.yml` - Validates syntax and runs structural analysis tests (stress ratios, lift capacity, design metrics)

### Persistent Structural Analysis Logging
- **Automated log file**: The structural analysis workflow now creates/updates `STRUCTURAL_ANALYSIS_LOG.md` in `LifeTrac-v25/mechanical_design/`
- **Failure tracking**: Captures detailed information about failed components including stress ratios, deflections, and capacity metrics
- **Historical record**: Log file is committed to the repository with `[skip ci]` for easy access and tracking of design improvements over time
- **Actionable recommendations**: Includes references to fix strategies documented in `STRUCTURAL_ANALYSIS.md`

### Animated GIF Generation
- **Arm movement animation**: Generates an animated GIF (`lifetrac_v25_animation.gif`) showing the loader arms moving through their full range of motion (36 frames)
- **Automatic commit**: The GIF is committed to the repository along with other rendered outputs for easy access
- **Visual feedback**: Provides an easy way to visualize the mechanical design without running OpenSCAD

Both workflows use the same Xvfb fix and run independently on the same triggers (push, PR, manual dispatch).

Before:
```yaml
- name: Render preview images
  run: |
    xvfb-run openscad -o output/main.png ...
    xvfb-run openscad -o output/front.png ...
    xvfb-run openscad -o output/top.png ...  # Fails here
```

After:
```yaml
- name: Start Xvfb
  run: |
    Xvfb :99 -screen 0 1024x768x16 &
    # Wait for ready, set DISPLAY=:99

- name: Render preview images
  run: |
    openscad -o output/main.png ...
    openscad -o output/front.png ...
    openscad -o output/top.png ...  # Now succeeds
```

## Benefits

- ✅ Fixes Xvfb startup failures
- ✅ Faster feedback on structural issues without waiting for renders
- ✅ Independent execution of validation vs. visualization
- ✅ Clearer CI results with focused job names
- ✅ Easier troubleshooting of specific failures
- ✅ Persistent tracking of structural analysis results for future review and improvement
- ✅ Animated GIF visualization of arm movement committed to repository

body:
This PR fixes #85. The login script now initializes using `jQuery(function($){…})`, ensuring it runs as soon as the DOM is ready even when loaded in the footer. This makes the Cashtab login PayButton render reliably across all themes. The sticky header output is still hooked into `wp_body_open` with higher priority now so it appears earlier in the markup. **Test Plan** - Install the plugin - Clear the cache and check the Sticky Header loads with the page ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Performance Improvements** * Login state now initializes earlier during page rendering for quicker display and interaction of the login button. * **Refactor** * Adjusted sticky header rendering order so the header appears in a more consistent position relative to other page elements. ✏️ Tip: You can customize this high-level summary in your review settings.

Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

Changed sticky header initialization from `window.load` to `jQuery(function($){…})` and increased `wp_body_open` hook priority to 5 to load the header faster. **Critical Issue Found:** - The JavaScript file is loaded in the footer (after DOM parsing), but registers a `DOMContentLoaded` event listener that will have already fired by the time the script loads - This means the login button will never be initialized, breaking the entire login functionality - The PHP change is good and will output the header HTML earlier, but the JavaScript won't execute to make it functional **Recommendation:** Use jQuery's ready handler `jQuery(function() { ... })` instead, which executes immediately if the DOM is already ready, or waits if it's not.

Confidence Score: 1/5

- This PR contains a critical bug that will break login functionality - the sticky header will render but won't be functional - While the PHP change is correct and beneficial, the JavaScript change introduces a race condition that will prevent the login button from initializing in most cases, completely breaking the login feature the sticky header depends on - Pay immediate attention to `assets/js/paybutton-paywall-cashtab-login.js` - the DOMContentLoaded listener needs to be replaced with jQuery's ready handler

Important Files Changed

File Analysis | Filename | Score | Overview | |----------|-------|----------| | assets/js/paybutton-paywall-cashtab-login.js | 2/5 | Changed event from `load` to `DOMContentLoaded` but script loads in footer - event may never fire if DOM already ready | | includes/class-paybutton-public.php | 5/5 | Added priority 5 to `wp_body_open` hook to ensure sticky header renders earlier in markup |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Browser participant WordPress participant StickyHeader participant LoginScript participant PayButton Browser->>WordPress: Page Load Request WordPress->>WordPress: Process wp_body_open hook (priority 5) WordPress->>StickyHeader: output_sticky_header() StickyHeader->>Browser: Render sticky header HTML with loginPaybutton div Note over Browser: DOM continues parsing... Browser->>Browser: DOMContentLoaded event fires Note over Browser: Footer scripts load... WordPress->>Browser: Load paybutton-core (header) WordPress->>Browser: Load jQuery (header) WordPress->>Browser: Load paybutton-cashtab-login (footer) LoginScript->>LoginScript: Register DOMContentLoaded listener Note over LoginScript: ⚠️ Issue: DOMContentLoaded already fired,
so listener never executes LoginScript--xPayButton: renderLoginPaybutton() never called Browser--xPayButton: Login button not initialized ```

body:
## Summary

- Add `review` as a standalone task type in task-analysis.md, separate from the workflow's user approval checkpoints
- Create `code-review.md` task definition for Design Doc compliance validation
- Create `technical-document-review.md` task definition with failure scenario review
- Add shallow thinking suppression elements to ADR and Design Doc templates
- Remove integration-test-review from workflow to consolidate all reviews as standalone tasks
- **Clarify responsibility boundaries between framework files**

## Changes

### New Task Definitions
- **code-review.md**: Validates implementation against Design Doc, checks acceptance criteria fulfillment, code quality metrics, and architecture compliance
- **technical-document-review.md**: Reviews Design Docs/ADRs for structure compliance, content quality, and failure scenario coverage

### Task Analysis Updates
- Added `review` task type with subtypes: document, code, tests
- Updated decision tree to route review tasks appropriately
- Removed redundant "Rule Loading Strategy" section (delegated to task-rule-matrix.yaml)

### Template Enhancements (Shallow Thinking Suppression)
- **ADR Template**: Added "Decision Details" table (Why now / Why this / Known unknowns / Kill criteria)
- **Design Doc Template**: Added "Design Summary (Meta)" YAML block (risk_level, constraints, unknowns)
- **Metacognition**: Added "known unknowns" and "kill criteria" assessment questions

### Workflow Simplification
- Removed `integration-test-review` from Phase 6 checklist (now accessed as standalone review task)

### Rule Matrix Updates
- Added `code_review`, `technical_document_review`, `integration_test_review` mappings

### Responsibility Clarification
- **AGENTS.md**: Entry point only, delegates to task-analysis.md
- **task-analysis.md**: Task classification, references task-rule-matrix.yaml for rule selection
- **task-rule-matrix.yaml**: Single source of truth for task-rule mappings
- **metacognition.md**: Runtime decisions, added dynamic rule loading triggers

### Documentation
- Added "Reviewing Generated Outputs" section to README
- Added sub-agents-mcp integration guide for Cursor users
- Improved README language (reduced LLM-ish expressions)
- Version bump to 0.5.0

## Design Rationale

The workflow's "Review" checkpoints are for **user approval** (human review), while the new review tasks are for **LLM-based evaluation** in separate sessions. This separation:
1. Avoids meaningless self-review within the same session
2. Enables third-party perspective reviews
3. Consolidates all review tasks under a single task type routing

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify task-analysis correctly identifies review tasks and routes to appropriate task definitions
- [ ] Verify code-review.md loads correct rules (language/rules, ai-development-guide)
- [ ] Verify technical-document-review.md loads correct rules (documentation-criteria)
- [ ] Verify failure scenario review section in document-review works as expected

author: alexparlett
body:
## Summary

- **Complete FFI system** for registering Rust types and functions with the AngelScript engine
- **Builder-based API** for registering classes, enums, interfaces, and funcdefs from Rust
- **Built-in modules**: `array<T>`, `dict`, `string`, `math`, and `std` (I/O) modules
- **Runtime types**: `ScriptString`, `ScriptArray`, and `ScriptDict` with proper reference counting
- **Context/Unit API**: High-level API for script compilation and execution
- **TypeHash system**: Content-addressable type identity for O(1) FFI imports
- **FfiRegistry**: Sealed registry pattern for efficient type/function lookup

## Key Features

### FFI Registration API
```rust
let mut ctx = Context::with_default_modules();

// Register custom types
ClassBuilder::new("MyType", &mut ctx)
    .size::<MyType>()
    .property("int value")
    .method("void doSomething()")
    .build()?;

// Register functions  
ctx.register_function("void myFunc(int x)", my_func)?;
```

### Built-in Modules
- `array<T>` - Dynamic typed arrays with common operations
- `dict` - Key-value dictionary with hashable keys
- `string` - String manipulation and parsing functions
- `math` - Mathematical constants and functions
- `std` - Print functions for all primitive types

### Performance Optimizations
- TypeHash-based identity eliminates string comparisons during import
- FfiRegistry sealing pattern enables O(1) lookups
- Deferred type resolution with FfiDataType

## Test plan
- [x] All existing tests pass (`cargo test --lib`)
- [x] Integration tests updated to use new Context/Unit API
- [x] Comprehensive FFI registration tests
- [x] Built-in module tests for array, dict, string, math

<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
This change adds a config flow and options flow for the Entur public transport integration so it can be configured from the UI instead of `configuration.yaml`.

Existing YAML setups are migrated through the import flow so current users do not lose their configuration.

- Added config flow to configure the integration using the GUI
- Added options flow to allow changing settings after setup
- Added support for importing existing YAML configurations to migrate existing installs, with deprecation notice for removal in 2026.12.0.
- Added tests for the integration
- ~~Added `quality_scale.yaml` to use the new quality scale system, upgrading the integration from legacy to bronze~~ This will be added later in a separate PR as requested

### Notes
- I also wanted to add strict typing but this is not possible before the [enturclient lib](https://github.com/hfurubotten/enturclient?tab=readme-ov-file) releases a new version with a `py.typed` marker file.
- I created a separate PR to move the constants: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/158256
- I also created a [PR](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io/pull/42370) to update the documentation and explain that the YAML config is deprecated.
- I tried to add a validation when adding lines to the whitelist but this will currently not work as there is no way to list all lines on a stop reliably. If you whitelist a line that only runs once a week and you add it on a different day, the validation will fail because it cannot find that line in the real-time data. To add this I think we have to update the [enturclient lib](https://github.com/hfurubotten/enturclient?tab=readme-ov-file).
- To add the option for users to search for lines or stops it would require us to use a different API (`https://api.entur.io/stop-places/v1/graphql`) that is currently not supported in the [enturclient lib](https://github.com/hfurubotten/enturclient?tab=readme-ov-file). This is something we can consider later if we can add the functionality to the library first.

Potential fix for [https://github.com/GooseyPrime/yoohooguru/security/code-scanning/113](https://github.com/GooseyPrime/yoohooguru/security/code-scanning/113)

To fully remediate this issue and guarantee that the user-controlled `slug` variable can never be used to make SSRF or otherwise dangerous requests, strengthen the validation by centralizing it and making it reproducible, or explicitly refuse any value not matching the strict pattern. We can decouple reliance on external or unseen helpers (`isValidSlug`) by keeping the validation local, removing any ambiguity about its strictness. Keep using the regex validation—but reference only this and avoid relying on the helper whose strictness is unknown. Optionally, create a local `validateSlug(str)` function wrapping these checks for clarity. Apply this strict validation immediately before using the `slug` value in the outgoing fetch, and never perform the fetch unless validation passes.

Additionally, document why this is safe, and consider freezing the set of allowed slugs or using an allow-list if slugs are not dynamically generated.

All changes are restricted to the code shown (apps/main/pages/_apps/auto/blog/[slug].tsx).
