body:
# 🚀 Fix: "Edit Task" menu action not working in Table View

## Description

This PR fixes a bug where the "Edit Task" action in the team member row menu works correctly in Card and Block views, but does nothing in the Table view.

- **Problem:** Clicking "Edit Task" in the Table view menu failed to trigger edit mode on the task cell.
- **Root Cause:** State isolation caused by multiple React hook instances. Each cell component (`TaskCell`, `ActionMenuCell`) independently called `useTMCardTaskEdit()`, creating separate hook instances with isolated `editMode` state.
- **Solution:** Implemented a React Context pattern to share hook instances across all cells in the same table row, ensuring they all use the same `taskEdition` state.

## What Was Changed

### Major Changes

- **`apps/web/core/components/pages/teams/team/team-members-views/user-team-table/team-member-cells.tsx`**
  - Created `TeamMemberRowContext` to share `memberInfo` and `taskEdition` state across cells
  - Created `useTeamMemberRowContext()` hook for cells to consume shared state
  - Created `TeamMemberRowProviderInternal` (memoized) that creates hooks once per row
  - Created `TeamMemberRowWrapper` component compatible with DataTable's `rowWrapper` prop
  - Modified `TaskCell`, `WorkedOnTaskCell`, `TaskEstimateInfoCell`, `ActionMenuCell` to use shared context

- **`apps/web/core/components/common/data-table.tsx`**
  - Added `rowWrapper` optional prop to `DataTableProps` interface
  - Modified row rendering to conditionally wrap cells with the provided wrapper component

- **`apps/web/core/components/pages/teams/team/team-members-views/user-team-table/team-members-table-view.tsx`**
  - Added import for `TeamMemberRowWrapper`
  - Passed `rowWrapper={TeamMemberRowWrapper}` prop to DataTable component

### Minor Changes

- Removed unused `row` parameter from cell components that now use context
- Added JSDoc comments explaining the context pattern and its purpose

## How to Test This PR

1. Run the app with `yarn web:dev`
2. Open the browser at `http://localhost:3030`
3. Navigate to a Team page with members
4. Switch to **Table view** using the view toggle
5. Click the three-dot menu (⋮) on any team member row
6. Click "Edit Task"
7. ✅ Verify the task cell shows an input field for editing
8. Type a task name and press Enter to save
9. Verify the task is updated correctly

**Regression tests:**
- Switch to **Card view** → Click menu → "Edit Task" → Should still work
- Switch to **Block view** → Click menu → "Edit Task" → Should still work
- Test "Edit Estimate" in Table view → Should work correctly

## Screenshots (if needed)

| Before | After |
| ------ | ----- |
| Clicking "Edit Task" in Table view does nothing | Task cell correctly switches to edit mode |

### Previous screenshots

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a98a8a32-54b3-4373-b469-c6b182de17ba

### Current screenshots

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/74552c98-9167-4290-be98-5b1be66c7403

## Related Issues

- [ETP-211 [Web]-[Bug] "Edit Task" Menu Action Not Working in Table View](https://evertech.atlassian.net/browse/ETP-211?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiODM2YmNkY2M2YzljNDk4OGI3YWRjZjQyMTdjZmRmNDIiLCJwIjoiamlyYS1zbGFjay1pbnQifQ)

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (fixes a problem)
- [ ] New feature (adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (requires changes elsewhere)
- [ ] Documentation update

## ✅ Checklist

- [x] My code follows the project coding style
- [x] I reviewed my own code and added comments where needed
- [x] I tested my changes locally
- [x] I updated or created related documentation if needed
- [x] No new warnings or errors are introduced

## Notes for the Reviewer (Optional)

- The `rowWrapper` prop added to DataTable is generic and can be reused for other tables needing shared row state
- The Context pattern follows the same approach used in the Card view (`user-team-card/index.tsx`) where a single `taskEdition` instance is shared
- `UserInfoCell` still creates its own `memberInfo` as it doesn't need shared state and requires `publicTeam` from cell meta

### Technical Context

The root cause was that `useTMCardTaskEdit` uses `useState` internally:

```typescript
// In use-team-member-card.ts
const [editMode, setEditMode] = useState(false);
```

Each hook call creates new independent state. The Context pattern ensures all cells in a row share the same hook instance.

```

author: harshitsaini17
body:
# fix: shuffle should report nullability correctly

- Replace return_type with return_field_from_args to preserve input nullability
- Add test to verify nullability is correctly reported
- Addresses issue #19145

## Which issue does this PR close?

Closes #19145

## Rationale for this change

The `shuffle` UDF was using the default `is_nullable` implementation which always returns `true`, regardless of the input array's nullability. This causes:
1. Incorrect schema inference - non-nullable inputs are incorrectly marked as nullable
2. Missed optimization opportunities - the query optimizer cannot apply certain optimizations when nullability information is incorrect
3. Potential runtime errors - incorrect metadata can lead to unexpected behavior in downstream operations

The shuffle function simply reorders elements within an array without changing the array's structure or nullability, so the output should have the same nullability as the input.

## What changes are included in this PR?

1. **Implemented `return_field_from_args`**: Returns the input field directly, preserving both data type and nullability
2. **Updated `return_type`**: Now returns an error directing users to use `return_field_from_args` instead (following DataFusion best practices)
3. **Added comprehensive tests**: Verifies that both nullable and non-nullable inputs are handled correctly

## Are these changes tested?

Yes, this PR includes a new test `test_shuffle_nullability` that verifies:
- Non-nullable array input produces non-nullable output
- Nullable array input produces nullable output
- Data types are preserved correctly in both cases

author: tagorr
body:
Summary

This pull request refines the ADSI-based password handling for the long-lived `primaryadmin` account, building on top of PR #54 (`sec: use ADSI for primaryadmin password and align security docs`).

It closes the gap where an ADSI failure after `net user /add` could leave a newly created `primaryadmin` account without a securely applied password.

Details

Code changes (CreatePrimaryAdmin.ps1):

* Stage A now wraps the `Set-L2CLocalUserPasswordAdsi` call in a try/catch when creating `primaryadmin`.
* If ADSI password setting fails after `net user <PrimaryUser> /add` succeeds:

  * Stage A logs `Failed to set password via ADSI for <user>: <error>`.
  * The script attempts rollback via `net user <user> /delete`, logs the delete return code (`Rolled back user ... after password failure (delete rc=...)` or an equivalent failure log), and then throws.
  * Stage A fails closed and forces the Stage B recovery path.
* When `primaryadmin` already existed before Stage A:

  * Stage A calls `Set-L2CLocalUserPasswordAdsi` without touching `net.exe`.
  * On ADSI failure, Stage A logs the error, logs `Skipping deletion because <user> existed before this run`, and throws.
  * No deletion is attempted for pre-existing accounts; the existing admin is preserved, but the run still fails closed.

Documentation changes:

* DECISIONS.md (ADR-010): documents the exact Stage A flows for newly created vs pre-existing `primaryadmin`, including ADSI failure handling and rollback behavior.
* SECURITY.md: clarifies that the `primaryadmin` password never goes through `net.exe` command-line arguments, is applied exclusively via the WinNT ADSI provider, and describes the fail-closed, observable handling of ADSI failures in both the “new account” and “existing account” cases.
* docs/AUDIT_CHECKLIST.md: adds a negative test for a simulated ADSI password failure for `primaryadmin`, including expected evidence in `SetupComplete.log`, `C:\ProgramData\l2c_master_*.log`, and the resulting VM state (no `primaryadmin` in Administrators, `bootstrap` and secrets preserved for investigation).

Outcome

With this change:

* The `primaryadmin` password remains off process command lines and out of Security 4688 events (via ADSI-only password application).
* A failed ADSI password operation for a newly created `primaryadmin` cannot silently leave a half-configured admin account; the account is rolled back, and the run enters recovery mode.
* For a pre-existing `primaryadmin`, ADSI failures are logged, the account is preserved, and Stage A still fails closed, with recovery logs clearly indicating the failure reason.

body:
Four critical production issues prevented long-running autonomous pentesting missions: unbounded memory growth, regex-based command validation vulnerable to bypass, subprocess output exhausting RAM, and strategy repetition blindness.

## Memory Leak Prevention

Replaced unbounded collections with fixed-size circular buffers:

```python
# Before: unbounded lists grow forever
self.context_history = []
self.error_patterns = {}

# After: bounded deques with auto-pruning
from collections import deque
self.context_history = deque(maxlen=1000)
self.recent_errors = deque(maxlen=50)

# Prune error_patterns when > 500 entries (keep top 200 by frequency)
if len(self.error_patterns) > ERROR_PATTERNS_MAX_SIZE:
    self.error_patterns = dict(sorted_errors[:ERROR_PATTERNS_KEEP_COUNT])
```

## Security Bypass Hardening

Replaced weak regex with `shlex.split()` for proper shell parsing:

```python
# Before: bypassed by flag reordering or spacing
if re.search(r'rm\s+-rf', command):
    flag_dangerous()

# After: parse flags correctly, check all variants
tokens = shlex.split(command)
base_cmd, args = tokens[0], tokens[1:]
if base_cmd == 'rm':
    has_recursive = '-r' in args or '-R' in args or '-rf' in ''.join(args)
    has_force = '-f' in args or '-rf' in ''.join(args)
    has_critical = any(arg in CRITICAL_PATHS for arg in args)
```

Detects: `-rf`, `-fr`, `-r -f`, `--recursive --force`, extra spaces, full paths.

## Output Bomb Protection

Replaced `communicate()` with chunked reading and byte limits:

```python
# Before: loads entire output into RAM
stdout, stderr = await process.communicate()

# After: read in chunks, kill if exceeds limit
async def _safe_run_command(cmd, timeout, max_bytes=5MB):
    for chunk in read_chunks(4096):
        total_bytes += len(chunk)
        if total_bytes > max_bytes:
            process.kill()
            raise RuntimeError("Output bomb detected")
```

Applied to all subprocess calls: `checksec`, `file`, `readelf`, `objdump`.

## Semantic Loop Detection

Added error classification to detect strategy repetition:

```python
# Before: only detected exact action duplication
action_hash = hash(json.dumps(action))

# After: track (tool, error_class) patterns
def _detect_semantic_loop(action, error):
    error_class = classify_error(error)  # "forbidden", "not_found", etc.
    self.recent_errors.append((action['tool'], error_class))
    
    # Trigger if same (tool, error) appears 3+ times in last 5 actions
    if recent_errors.count((tool, error_class)) >= 3:
        return True  # Pivot strategy
```

Catches: SQL injection repeated 50x with different payloads but same "403" error.

**Files Modified:**
- `agents/multi_llm_orchestrator.py`: Memory management, semantic loops
- `agents/cognitive_mechanisms.py`: Command validation with shlex
- `tools/capabilities/pwn_exploiter.py`: Chunked subprocess output

> You are an Expert AI Software Architect and Senior Security Engineer. I have a Python-based autonomous pentesting agent (Aegis v8.0) that needs a critical "Production-Readiness" refactor. The current code has 4 fatal flaws: memory leaks, security bypasses, process crashes, and logic blind spots.
> 
> Your task is to fix these 4 specific issues by modifying the code as described below. Do not remove existing functionality, only harden it.
> 
> ### 1. FIX MEMORY LEAKS in `agents/multi_llm_orchestrator.py`
> **The Issue:** The `MultiLLMOrchestrator` uses unbounded lists (`self.context_history`) and dictionaries (`self.error_patterns`) that grow forever, causing crashes in long missions.
> **The Fix:**
> - Import `collections.deque`.
> - Change `self.context_history` to a `deque(maxlen=1000)`.
> - Change `self.recent_errors` to a `deque(maxlen=50)` (or similar rolling window).
> - Implement a cleanup routine in `_initialize_usage_tracker` that prunes `self.error_patterns` if it exceeds 500 entries (keeping only frequently occurring errors).
> 
> ### 2. FIX SECURITY BYPASS in `agents/cognitive_mechanisms.py`
> **The Issue:** The `PreExecutionAuditor` uses weak Regex (`r'rm\s+-rf'`) to stop dangerous commands. Attackers can bypass this by swapping flags (e.g., `rm -fr /`) or adding extra spaces.
> **The Fix:**
> - Import `shlex`.
> - Rewrite `_check_dangerous_patterns`. Instead of Regex, use `shlex.split(command)` to parse the command into a list of arguments.
> - logic: If the base command is `rm`, iterate through the args. If you detect BOTH recursive flags (`-r`, `-R`, `--recursive`) AND force flags (`-f`, `--force`) combined with a critical target path (`/`, `/bin`, etc), flag it as dangerous immediately.
> 
> ### 3. FIX PROCESS CRASHES ("Output Bombs") in `tools/capabilities/pwn_exploiter.py`
> **The Issue:** The tool uses `await process.communicate()` which loads the entire stdout into RAM. A malicious binary printing infinite text will crash the agent.
> **The Fix:**
> - Create a helper method `_safe_run_command(cmd, timeout, max_bytes=5*1024*1024)`.
> - Use `asyncio.subprocess.PIPE` and read the stream chunk-by-chunk (e.g., 4KB chunks).
> - Keep a running total of bytes read. If the total exceeds `max_bytes` (5MB), kill the process immediately and raise an error.
> 
> ### 4. FIX LOGIC BLIND SPOTS in `agents/multi_llm_orchestrator.py`
> **The Issue:** The loop detector only hashes exact command strings. It fails to notice "Semantic Loops" where the agent tries the same *strategy* (e.g., SQL injection) 50 times with slightly different payloads but gets the same error every time.
> **The Fix:**
> - Implement `_detect_semantic_loop`.
> - Instead of hashing the full action, track a sequence of `(tool_name, error_type)` tuples.
> - If the last 3-5 actions use the same tool and result in the same error class (e.g., "403 Forbidden"), trigger the loop handler even if the arguments are different.
>

- **Dynamic Y-axis scaling** - Step size adapts to inventory range (5/10/20) based on max values to prevent overcrowded or sparse tick marks.

- **SSR-safe rendering** - DOM access gated by `import.meta.client` following Nuxt patterns established in InventoryProjectionChart.

- **Dashboard integration** - Added to `pages/index.vue` above the existing InventoryProjectionChart.

```typescript
// Key chart data structure
chartData.value = {
  labels: validCookies.map((cookie) => cookie.abbreviation), // Uses abbreviations: TM, ADV, LEM
  datasets: [
    {
      type: 'bar' as const,
      label: 'On Hand',
      data: validCookies.map((cookie) => cookie.onHand || 0),
      backgroundColor: validCookies.map((cookie) => cookie.color || '#888'),
    },

};

// Individual horizontal lines for each bar via annotations
annotations[`afterPending_${cookie.abbreviation}`] = {
  type: 'line',

  xMax: index + 0.4,

  yMax: afterPending,
  borderColor: '#6b7280',

};

author: copilot
body:
Addresses 5 critical issues in the KOReader BookStack plugin: placeholder file deletion bug during auto-download, missing standard OPDS series metadata support, lack of orphaned placeholder cleanup, no metadata change detection during sync, and inefficient sync UI for large libraries.

## Download Bug Fix

**Root cause**: Placeholder document remained open during download, causing file lock that prevented deletion. Downloaded book was deleted instead of placeholder.

**Changes**:
- Close `ReaderUI.instance` before initiating download in `handlePlaceholderAutoDownload()`
- Use timestamped temp files (`filename.downloading_<timestamp>.tmp`) to prevent conflicts
- Verify temp file creation before deleting placeholder

```lua
-- Close document FIRST to avoid file locks
if ReaderUI.instance then
    UIManager:close(ReaderUI.instance)
    ReaderUI.instance = nil
end
UIManager:scheduleIn(Constants.DOCUMENT_CLOSE_DELAY, function()
    self:downloadFromPlaceholderAuto(filepath, book_info)
end)
```

## OPDS Series Metadata Support

Added priority-based series extraction in `parseBookloreOPDSFeed()`:

1. `belongs-to-collection` + `group-position` (EPUB 3/OPDS 2.0 standard)
2. `calibre:series` + `calibre:series_index` (Calibre compatibility)
3. Publisher field (existing behavior, backward compatible)
4. Summary field `|Series #N|` (fallback)

Standard OPDS fields now take precedence; publisher-based extraction still works when enabled.

## Library Sync Enhancements

### Orphan Cleanup
- Build book ID lookup from remote library
- Identify and delete local placeholders for removed books
- Report deletion count in sync summary

### Metadata Change Detection
`syncLibrary()` now performs two-pass sync:
1. **Cleanup pass**: Remove orphaned placeholders
2. **Update pass**: Compare stored metadata (title, author, series, series_index) against remote; regenerate placeholders when changed

Handles filename updates when series information changes.

```lua
if existing_info.title ~= book.title or
   existing_info.series ~= book.series or
   existing_info.series_index ~= book.series_index then
    -- Delete and regenerate with new metadata
    os.remove(filepath)
    PlaceholderGenerator:createMinimalEPUB(book, new_filepath)
end
```

## Cover Import Improvements

- Configurable 5s timeout (`Constants.COVER_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT`)
- 6 URL extraction patterns for better OPDS feed compatibility
- Minimum size validation (100 bytes) to detect failed downloads
- Accept HTTP 304 status

## Sync UI Optimization

- Removed confirmation dialog in `buildPlaceholderLibrary()`
- Progress updates every 100 items (previously 5) for large libraries
- Force UI repaint for real-time feedback
- Enhanced summary: created, updated, skipped, failed, orphans removed

All magic numbers extracted to `constants.lua` for maintainability.

author: breenyoung
body:
### 🔧 Fix: Kavita "Virtual Volume" Collision Workaround

**The Problem:**
Kavita deviates from standard comic schemas by putting non-standard issues (Annuals, Specials) into a single "Virtual Volume" (often named `100000` or Volume `0`) instead of creating distinct Volume entities.
* **Result:** This caused a hash collision in our migration map. "Superman 6" (Regular) and "Superman Annual 6" (Virtual Vol 0) would both map to the key `superman|6`, causing the Annual to overwrite the Regular issue in the import logic.

**The Solution:**
We updated `KavitaMigrationService` to respect `format` as a distinct entity key.

1.  **Split Namespace:** The migration map now generates composite keys using `is_special` status: `series|number|is_special`.
2.  **Format Detection (Parker Side):** We import the centralized `NON_PLAIN_FORMATS` list to automatically flag Parker comics as "Special" if their format is 'Annual', 'One-Shot', 'TPB', etc.
3.  **Virtual Volume Detection (Kavita Side):** We inspect the Kavita `Volume` table for the signature `100000` name or `0` number to identify items in the "Specials Bucket."
4.  **Result:** "Superman 6" maps to `superman|6|False` and "Superman Annual 6" maps to `superman|6|True`. Both import correctly with no data loss.

author: qnope
body:
## Summary

- **Remove position buffer from GBuffer**: World positions are now reconstructed from the depth buffer using an inverse view-projection matrix, reducing memory bandwidth and storage requirements
- **Implement depth-based position reconstruction in sun light pass**: Added shader-side position reconstruction with distance-adaptive shadow bias for numerical stability at large world coordinates
- **Remove legacy VulkanExample class (~400 lines)**: The Advanced example now uses the RayTracedScene abstraction, demonstrating the intended high-level API usage pattern
- **Add documentation for screenshot testing**: Document SDL_VULKAN_LIBRARY setup for macOS with vcpkg

## Technical Details

### GBuffer Optimization
The explicit world position buffer has been removed from the GBuffer. Instead, positions are reconstructed in the lighting pass using:
```glsl
vec4 worldPos = inverseViewProj * clipPos;
return worldPos.xyz / worldPos.w;
```

This trades a small amount of compute for reduced memory bandwidth, which is typically beneficial on modern GPUs.

### Shadow Ray Improvements
- Distance-adaptive bias: `max(0.1, length(position) * 0.0005)` prevents shadow acne at large coordinates
- Extended ray distance (tMax: 100001) for large scenes like Sponza
- Added ambient light term (0.2) for shadowed areas

## Test plan
- [ ] Build the project with `cmake --build build-Clang20Debug`
- [ ] Run the Advanced example to verify Sponza renders correctly with ray-traced shadows
- [ ] Verify shadow quality at different sun angles

It removes usage of test constants and centralizes chain-specific values, improving maintainability and reducing errors. Additionally, EVM and ERC20 module initialization and upgrade handlers are updated to properly set and initialize denom metadata and options.

author: copilot
body:
Built a complete Flask web application that converts bank statement PDFs into Excel files with intelligent line grouping by similarity. Users can register accounts, create projects, and upload PDFs that are automatically processed to group similar transactions.

## Architecture

- **Database Models**: User, Project, PDFFile with cascade deletion
- **Authentication**: Flask-Login with Werkzeug password hashing
- **API Layer**: REST endpoints for all operations (registration, login, project CRUD, file management)
- **Processing**: pdfplumber for text extraction, difflib.SequenceMatcher for similarity matching (0.8 threshold)
- **Output**: Styled Excel with representative lines, occurrence counts, and grouped variations

## Core Algorithm

```python
def group_similar_lines(self, lines):
    groups = []
    used_indices = set()
    
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if i in used_indices:
            continue
        
        group = [line]
        used_indices.add(i)
        
        for j, other_line in enumerate(lines):
            if j <= i or j in used_indices:
                continue
            
            if SequenceMatcher(None, line.lower(), other_line.lower()).ratio() >= 0.8:
                group.append(other_line)
                used_indices.add(j)
        
        groups.append((line, group, len(group)))
    
    return sorted(groups, key=lambda x: x[2], reverse=True)
```

## Security

- Debug mode disabled in production via `FLASK_ENV` environment variable
- `SECRET_KEY` configurable via environment (no hardcoded secrets)
- File validation: PDF only, 16MB limit
- Session-based authentication with secure cookies

## API Endpoints

```bash
POST   /auth/api/register           # Create user account
POST   /auth/api/login              # Authenticate and create session
GET    /projects/api/projects       # List user's projects
POST   /projects/api/projects       # Create new project
GET    /projects/api/projects/{id}  # Get project with files
DELETE /projects/api/projects/{id}  # Delete project and files
POST   /projects/{id}/upload        # Upload and process PDF
GET    /projects/download/{file_id} # Download Excel output
```

- 22 lines extracted → 10 unique groups
- Correctly grouped: 5 "Payment to ABC Corporation", 3 "ATM Withdrawal", 3 "Transfer to", 3 "Payment to XYZ Services", 3 "Payment to Utility Company"

author: enterthearcane
body:
## What does this PR do?

This change resolves several compilation errors that occur when building the engine with a C++23 toolchain. O3DE currently targets C++20, but these updates improve forward compatibility by addressing issues already surfaced under C++23 without altering the engine's official standard version.

The primary source of failures was the use of forward-declared types inside `std::unique_ptr`. Under C++23, the default deleter requires a complete type in the translation unit where the unique pointer is instantiated. Several engine classes had defaulted constructors or destructors defined inline in headers, which caused incomplete-type errors once compiled with C++23. The affected constructors and destructors have been moved to implementation files so that the full type definitions are always visible when needed.

Additional fixes include:

* Replacing the use of `std::aligned_storage`, which is deprecated in C++23. To keep changes minimally invasive, `AZStd::aligned_storage` has been reimplemented following the possible implementation from cppreference, without refactoring existing call sites to a different pattern.
* Adjustments to test code to ensure variables are initialized where required by C++23's stricter rules.
* Minor cleanups involving unique pointers with default initialization. The logic for nullptr assignment construction and default construction is the same.
* Moving several inline factory or constructor definitions into implementation files to avoid incomplete-type instantiation issues.

These changes allow the engine itself to compile under C++23. Some external third-party packages still require updates before a complete C++23 build is possible. The following upstream fixes will need to be incorporated separately:

* googletest: https://github.com/google/googletest/commit/fa8438ae6b70c57010177de47a9f13d7041a6328
* pybind11: https://github.com/pybind/pybind11/pull/4136

## How was this PR tested?

I compiled the engine on Windows 11 using both MSVC and Clang (not clang-cl), with both unity and non-unity builds. The changes resolve the incomplete-type and `aligned_storage` errors encountered when enabling C++23 for the engine code. (Configuring using `-DCMAKE_CXX_STANDARD=23`)

The list wrapping regex was using [^<]* which failed to match list items containing HTML tags (like <strong> from bold text or <em> from italics). This left <li> elements orphaned without a parent <ul>/<ol>, causing them to display incorrectly against the left border.

Changed to .*? non-greedy match which correctly handles list items with any inline formatting (bold, italic, code, links).

author: copilot
body:
Replace Alpine-based single-stage build with a hardened multi-stage approach: Alpine builder for fetching/validating kubectl, scratch-based final image containing only the kubectl binary.

## Changes

### Dockerfile
- **Stage 1 (builder)**: Fetch kubectl from dl.k8s.io, verify SHA256 checksum, test binary
- **Stage 2 (final)**: `FROM scratch` with single `COPY --from=builder --chown=0:0 /build/kubectl /kubectl`
- Set `ENTRYPOINT ["/kubectl"]` (was `CMD ["kubectl"]`)

**Before:**
```dockerfile
FROM alpine:latest
RUN apk update && apk upgrade && apk add --no-cache curl ca-certificates
# ... download kubectl to /usr/local/bin/
CMD ["kubectl"]
```

**After:**
```dockerfile
FROM alpine:latest AS builder
RUN apk add --no-cache ca-certificates
WORKDIR /build
RUN wget -O kubectl "https://dl.k8s.io/release/${KUBECTL_VERSION}/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl" && \
    wget -O kubectl.sha256 "..." && \
    echo "$(cat kubectl.sha256)  kubectl" | sha256sum -c

FROM scratch
COPY --from=builder --chown=0:0 /build/kubectl /kubectl
ENTRYPOINT ["/kubectl"]
```

### Workflow & Documentation
- Updated image labels: "Alpine-based" → "Hardened minimal kubectl...with only kubectl binary (no shell)"
- Removed shell access examples from README
- Updated security documentation to reflect minimal attack surface

## Security Impact

| Aspect | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Base image | Alpine (~7.5 MB + packages) | scratch (0 bytes) |
| Executables | 100+ | 1 |
| Shell/package manager | ✓ | ✗ |
| Attack vectors | Multiple (sh, apk, wget) | kubectl only |

Final image is immutable at runtime with no tools for privilege escalation or lateral movement.

body:
## Summary
- Split rules-pr.md (1990 lines) into 7 focused files for 70% token reduction
- Integrate agent automation workflows from PR #21 into modular structure
- Enable granular lazy-loading (2000→590 lines avg per operation)
- Update AGENTS.md with 9 trigger contexts (8 updated + 1 new)
- Deprecate rules-pr.md with 30-day grace period

## Context

**Problem**: rules-pr.md had grown to 2000 lines, loading unnecessarily for all PR operations and mixing platform-neutral concepts with GitHub-specific automation.

**Solution**: Split into 7 modular files with granular lazy-loading via AGENTS.md trigger contexts.

**Combines**:
- PR #21: Agent automation workflows (review cycles, rebase, freshness monitoring)
- PR #22: Modular file structure (platform separation, lazy-loading)

## New File Structure

### Platform-Neutral
- **rules-pr-concepts.md** (~425 lines) - Platform-neutral PR workflows, stacked PRs, merge strategies

### GitHub-Specific
- **rules-github-pr.md** (~100 lines) - Basic GitHub PR operations (branch deletion, cleanup)

### Agent Automation
- **rules-github-agent-review.md** (~470 lines) - Review cycle automation, inline comment handling (MCP + gh CLI)
- **rules-github-agent-create.md** (~220 lines) - PR creation + description auto-generation
- **rules-github-agent-rebase.md** (~410 lines) - Proactive rebase workflows + branch freshness monitoring
- **rules-github-agent-merge.md** (~60 lines) - Post-merge cascade updates for stacked PRs
- **rules-github-agent-utils.md** (~215 lines) - Pre-commit hooks, CI checks, amend safety, troubleshooting

## Agent Automation Features (from PR #21)

1. **Review Cycle Automation** - Iterative review→fix→re-review until all comments resolved
2. **PR Description Generation** - Full diff analysis + ticket integration + test plan generation
3. **Proactive Rebase Workflows** - 3 workflows: pre-review freshness, post-parent-merge cascade, periodic monitoring
4. **Branch Freshness Monitoring** - Multi-tier staleness thresholds (<5, 5-10, >10, >20 commits) with AI conflict resolution
5. **Post-Merge Cascade** - Auto-detect child PRs and offer rebase after parent merge
6. **Workflow Coordination** - Pre-commit hook handling, CI check monitoring, amend safety checks

## AGENTS.md Updates

Updated 8 trigger contexts + added 1 new:
- `pull_request_workflows` → loads rules-pr-concepts.md + rules-github-pr.md
- `modifying_existing_pr` → loads rules-pr-concepts.md + rules-github-pr.md
- `pr_review_response` → loads rules-pr-concepts.md + rules-github-agent-review.md

- `pr_maintenance` → loads rules-pr-concepts.md + rules-github-agent-rebase.md
- `pr_review_request` → loads rules-pr-concepts.md + rules-github-agent-rebase.md
- **`agent_pr_creation` (NEW)** → loads rules-pr-concepts.md + rules-github-agent-create.md
- `post_merge_operations` → loads rules-github-agent-merge.md

## Benefits

- **70% token reduction**: 2000→590 lines avg per operation (~5640 tokens saved)
- **Granular lazy-loading**: Only load workflows relevant to current task
- **Platform separation**: Clear distinction between platform-neutral + GitHub-specific
- **Complete automation**: Full agent workflows from PR #21 integrated
- **Future extensibility**: Easy to add GitLab/Bitbucket support without affecting GitHub workflows
- **Easier maintenance**: Focused files easier to update and review

- [x] AGENTS.md updated with 9 trigger contexts
- [x] Cross-references updated in rules-git.md, rules-github.md, rules-core.md, rules-development.md, rules-ai_agents.md
- [x] rules-pr.md deprecated with migration guide
- [x] Commit message follows conventional commits format

- **Deprecated**: 2025-12-08
- **Grace period**: 30 days (references updated, but file kept for backwards compatibility)
- **Removal**: 2026-01-08 (rules-pr.md will be deleted)

Closes #22 (split rules-pr.md for lazy-loading efficiency)

## Summary
- Simplify address caching with a lightweight `CacheService` using normalized keys.
- Apply cache reuse in the validation controller to avoid duplicate validations.
- Add unit and integration coverage for cache behavior and note the service in README.

## Technical Details
- Cache normalizes keys (trim + lowercase) and exposes `remember` helper to store computed results.
- Validation controller uses `remember` to memoize parsed responses before returning JSON.
- New tests cover cache normalization, remember semantics, and controller reuse path; README documents cache role.

## Risks & Rollback
- Cache is in-memory only; cache will reset on restarts and does not evict entries.
- Normalizing keys may treat intentionally different-cased inputs as identical (trade-off for dedupe).
- Rollback by reverting this PR.

author: albertoscv
body:
## Summary

This PR implements **Issue 13 – "Integrate Post-Processing"** by applying the provided `postprocessor.py` module to the predicted dependency trees.  

The goal is to take the raw CoNLL-U output produced by the parser, fix malformed trees (orphan nodes, multiple roots, cycles), and save a **cleaned** CoNLL-U file suitable for final evaluation.

---

## Changes Introduced

1. **Post-processing step added after writing raw predictions**

   After `main.py` writes the first-pass predictions to `data/output.conllu` (Issue 12), we now:

   - Instantiate the post-processor.
   - Run it on the predicted file.
   - Save the cleaned trees to a new file (e.g. `data/output_clean.conllu`).

   Example integration at the end of `main.py`:

   ```python
   # -------------------------------------------------
   # Issue 12: Write predicted trees to CoNLL-U
   # -------------------------------------------------
   output_path = "data/output.conllu"
   reader.write_conllu_file(parsed_trees, output_path)
   print(f' Predicted trees written to "{output_path}"')

   # -------------------------------------------------
   # Issue 13: Post-process predicted trees
   # -------------------------------------------------
   from src.postprocessor import PostProcessor

   postprocessor = PostProcessor()

   # Read and fix malformed trees from the predicted file
   cleaned_trees = postprocessor.postprocess(output_path)

   # Save cleaned trees to a new CoNLL-U file
   cleaned_output_path = "data/output_clean.conllu"
   reader.write_conllu_file(cleaned_trees, cleaned_output_path)
   print(f' Cleaned trees written to "{cleaned_output_path}"')

body:
This pull request makes several updates to the distributed ImageNet training repository, focusing on code organization, documentation cleanup, and usability improvements. The main changes include refactoring utility scripts for generating ImageNet class lists, removing outdated documentation, and adding a new prediction script for model inference. Additionally, minor usability improvements and message cleanups were made in the training script.

**Code organization and utility scripts:**
* Moved and refactored the `generate_classes.py` script from the project root to `scripts/generate_classes.py`, standardizing its logic for generating `imagenet_classes.py` from `imagenet_dirs.txt`. The original version was removed from the root.
* Added a new script `scripts/generate_classes_imagenet200.py` for generating Tiny ImageNet class lists from `wnids.txt`, restoring the previous Tiny ImageNet logic as a separate utility.

**Documentation cleanup:**
* Removed the `README_metrics.md` and `README_service.md` documentation files, which described logging/metrics and systemd service deployment, respectively. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-043953c6f1464088cc457d087ee0b07f7534bf6a14a83c9d995d8b535663ed8eL1-L44) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-68d7ffa4820de711d9e2fc5a78e5297183a68ce360299463cc52d217d6a717c3L1-L58)

**New features and usability improvements:**
* Added a new script `scripts/predict.py` for running inference on images using a trained model checkpoint. This script loads the model, processes the image, and outputs the predicted class, synset, and confidence.
* Minor message cleanups in `src/dhtPeerImagenet.py` to remove emojis and clarify printed output, improving log readability. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a3978f4489fec08498eb9509fa9af4229aa7184bd227e47a6f7cf3492649a58eL276-R281) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a3978f4489fec08498eb9509fa9af4229aa7184bd227e47a6f7cf3492649a58eL303-R303) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a3978f4489fec08498eb9509fa9af4229aa7184bd227e47a6f7cf3492649a58eL312-R312) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-a3978f4489fec08498eb9509fa9af4229aa7184bd227e47a6f7cf3492649a58eL462-R472) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-a3978f4489fec08498eb9509fa9af4229aa7184bd227e47a6f7cf3492649a58eL490-L497)

**Other changes:**
* Updated the systemd service configuration to remove instructional comments, leaving only the necessary configuration lines.
* Removed unused imports from `src/datasets.py` to clean up the codebase.
* Added a new sample system metrics CSV file to `stats/`, showing collected resource usage during training.

author: daksh-coder26
body:
## Description

Fixes #3402

This PR implements safety checks for `save_to_disk` to prevent accidental data loss, addressing Issue #3402.

### What was happening before?
`save_to_disk` would silently overwrite existing files or even entire directories when given a path that already contained data. This behavior could lead to unexpected data loss for users.

### What this PR changes
- Added an `overwrite` flag (default `False`) to `save_to_disk`
- If the target path is a **directory**, raise `IsADirectoryError`
- If the target is an existing **file** and `overwrite=False`, emit a `UserWarning` before overwriting
- If `overwrite=True`, overwrite without warning
- Updated the docstring in `data_utils.py`
- Added 3 new unit tests in `test_data_utils.py`:
  - warns when overwriting an existing file with `overwrite=False`
  - no warning when `overwrite=True`
  - directory path raises `IsADirectoryError`

### Why this is important
This prevents accidental overwriting of user data and provides explicit control via the `overwrite` flag. 
The default behavior remains backward compatible while making destructive behavior more explicit and safer for users.

author: copilot
body:
The "Add Block" modal correctly filters modules via `SystemBlock.getFilteredModules(plan)`, but existing blocks on pages are displayed regardless of their module status. Disabled modules should be hidden in Builder, preview, and runtime.

## Changes

### Core filtering logic
- Added `SystemBlock.isModuleEnabled(moduleId, plan)` helper method
- Conservative fail-closed: returns `false` when plan is `null` (hides all WL modules by default)
- Centralizes filtering logic previously duplicated in preview/runtime

### SystemBlockPreview & SystemBlockRuntime
- Replaced local `_isModuleEnabled()` with centralized `SystemBlock.isModuleEnabled()`
- Returns `SizedBox.shrink()` when module is disabled
- Added filtering for `BlockType.module` with `moduleId`

### BuilderPagePreview
- Added optional `plan` parameter (dynamic type to avoid import cycles)
- Passes plan to `SystemBlockPreview` instances

### BuilderPageEditorScreen
- Passes `_restaurantPlan` (from `restaurantPlanUnifiedProvider`) to `BuilderPagePreview`

## Behavior

```dart
// Module enabled in plan → block renders
SystemBlock.isModuleEnabled('roulette', plan)  // true → renders

// Module disabled in plan → block hidden
SystemBlock.isModuleEnabled('loyalty', plan)   // false → SizedBox.shrink()

// Plan not loaded → all WL modules hidden (conservative)
SystemBlock.isModuleEnabled('roulette', null)  // false → SizedBox.shrink()
```

**Note**: Blocks remain in Firestore (visual filtering only). Users can manually delete if desired.

## Files changed
- `builder_block.dart` - Added helper method
- `system_block_preview.dart` - Updated filtering (+19/-28)
- `system_block_runtime.dart` - Updated filtering (+11/-23)
- `builder_page_preview.dart` - Added plan parameter
- `builder_page_editor_screen.dart` - Pass plan to preview
- `system_block_test.dart` - Added unit tests

> 
> Je veux donc un patch propre et minimal qui fait EXACTEMENT ceci :

author: copilot
body:
The temp file cleanup validation in `workers/process_document_background.py` was vulnerable to path traversal attacks. Malicious paths like `/tmp/../etc/passwd` could bypass the `startswith('/tmp')` check and delete arbitrary system files.

**Changes:**

- Use `os.path.realpath()` to resolve paths before validation, preventing traversal via `..` components
- Add trailing slashes to allowed directories (`/tmp/`, `/var/folders/`) to prevent bypass with similar names like `/tmp2`
- Pass validated `real_path` to cleanup function instead of original `temp_path`

```python
# Before
if temp_path and (temp_path.startswith('/tmp') or temp_path.startswith('/var/folders')):
    await async_cleanup_temp_file(temp_path)

# After
real_path = os.path.realpath(temp_path)
allowed_dirs = ['/tmp/', '/var/folders/']
is_valid = any(real_path.startswith(d) or real_path == d.rstrip('/') for d in allowed_dirs)
if is_valid:
    await async_cleanup_temp_file(real_path)
```

The fix blocks `/tmp/../etc/passwd` (resolves to `/etc/passwd`), `/tmp2/file.txt`, and other evasion attempts while allowing legitimate temp files.

body:
Addresses review feedback on PR #94 to strengthen imagemap parsing security and consistency.

**Security improvements:**
- Protocol validation now uses `urllib.parse.urlparse` with scheme checking instead of string prefix matching, preventing bypass via case variation (`httP://`) or whitespace padding
- Image URLs validated to prevent XSS via `javascript:` or `data:` schemes
- Removed `mailto:` from allowed protocols to prevent email harvesting vectors

**Bounds and consistency:**
- Stricter coordinate validation prevents CSS overflow: `left < 100`, `top < 100`, `left + width ≤ 100`, `top + height ≤ 100`
- Single-line imagemaps (no areas) now return empty string, consistent with empty content behavior
- Removed redundant HTML escaping of `style` attribute (constructed from validated floats only)

```python
# Before: bypassed with case variation
if not (image_url.startswith("http://") or image_url.startswith("https://")):
    return ""

# After: robust scheme validation
parsed = urlparse(image_url.strip())
if parsed.scheme.lower() not in ("http", "https"):
    return ""
```

GitHub Pages serves the site from `https://kevinb42O.github.io/diepio-style-rpg-gam/` but Vite was building assets with root-relative paths, causing all JS/CSS to 404 and produce a white screen.

## Changes

- Added `base: '/diepio-style-rpg-gam/'` to `vite.config.ts`

This configures Vite to prefix all asset paths with the repository name, matching GitHub Pages' subdirectory structure.

**Before:**
```html

```

**After:**
```html

The GitHub Actions workflow already deploys from `./dist` and requires no changes.

body:
Did a big overhaul focused on fixing long-standing performance problems and breaking apart old monolithic systems.

LODOctree

Rewrote the whole thing.

Old version had serious performance issues and weird edge cases.

New version is cleaner, predictable, and runs way faster.

LOD transitions are no longer a mess.

Marching & Shaders

Took the giant marching cubes / shader pipeline and dismantled it into smaller, focused pieces.

Everything is now organized instead of crammed together.

Much easier to read, debug, and extend.

Started combining shader kernels and removing old cruft along the way.

Fixed a bunch of bugs hidden in the old structure (inverted densities, missing init, etc.).

Coloring / Terrain Data

Reworked how colors are packed and processed.

Cleaned up the terrain material and removed old arguments.

Early steps toward a better, consistent coloring system.

General Cleanup

Consolidated configs, renamed old base classes, removed dead systems.

Removed LINQ, obsolete functions, and random artifacts from early development.

Moved shaders back into the Engine where they actually belong.

Overall:
Huge improvement to performance, readability, and maintainability.
The core systems no longer fight me every time I touch them.

Implements user registration, authentication, and subscription management with a 30-day free trial followed by required $30/month Stripe payments.

## Core Implementation

**Authentication & User Management**
- Flask-Login session management with bcrypt password hashing
- User model tracks account creation date, Stripe customer/subscription IDs, and subscription status
- Email validation and password requirements (8+ characters)

**Subscription Logic**
- Accounts under 30 days old: free access
- Accounts over 30 days old: requires active Stripe subscription
- `@payment_required` decorator enforces subscription check on protected routes

**Stripe Integration**
- Checkout session creation for monthly subscriptions
- Webhook handler processes subscription lifecycle events (updated, canceled)
- Subscription status synced to database (active, canceled, past_due)
- Webhook signature verification required for security

## Security Hardening

- Removed fallback webhook processing without signature verification
- Debug mode and host binding controlled by environment configuration
- CSRF protection on all forms
- Sensitive configuration via environment variables

## Summary
This PR fixes several bugs in the `balance_inverters` function and adds comprehensive unit tests.

https://github.com/springfall2008/batpred/issues/3042

## Bug Fixes in `execute.py`

1. **Incorrect threshold variables**: Fixed usage of `balance_inverters_threshold_discharge` and `balance_inverters_threshold_charge` instead of incorrectly using `balance_inverters_discharge` and `balance_inverters_charge` (which are boolean enable flags, not thresholds)

2. **Swapped rate adjustment calls**: Fixed the cross-charging logic where `adjust_charge_rate` and `adjust_discharge_rate` calls were swapped

3. **dp0() on lists**: Fixed `dp0()` calls that were being applied to entire lists instead of individual values (now uses list comprehension `[dp0(x) for x in ...]`)

4. **Added test_mode parameter**: Added `test_mode` parameter to `balance_inverters()` to allow testing with pre-created inverters instead of always creating new ones

## New Tests

Added `test_balance_inverters.py` with 10 comprehensive test cases:
- Test 1: Low SoC inverter during discharge
- Test 2: High SoC inverter during charge
- Test 3: Cross charging during discharge
- Test 4: Cross discharging during charge
- Test 5: Already balanced inverters
- Test 6: Below threshold difference
- Test 7: Inverter at reserve during discharge
- Test 8: Balance disabled
- Test 9: Inverter in calibration mode
- Test 10: Insufficient power to balance

All balance_inverters tests pass:
```
./run_all --test balance_inverters

body:
## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved handling of workflows containing conditional blocks by preventing script generation errors and enabling graceful fallback processing. ✏️ Tip: You can customize this high-level summary in your review settings. ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Skip script generation for workflows with conditional blocks in `generate_workflow_script` to prevent caching divergent paths, with added logging for detection and errors. > > - **Behavior**: > - In `generate_workflow_script`, script generation is skipped for workflows with conditional blocks to prevent caching divergent paths. > - Logs a warning if conditional blocks are detected and script generation is skipped. > - Logs an error if block inspection fails, but continues with script generation. > - **Imports**: > - Added `get_all_blocks` and `BlockType` imports to handle block inspection. > - **Logging**: > - Added logging in `generate_workflow_script` to inform about conditional blocks and script generation status. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=Skyvern-AI%2Fskyvern&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for b6c9c86bf8de474e05fdb840adf59458171a4b33. You can [customize](https://app.ellipsis.dev/Skyvern-AI/settings/summaries) this summary. It will automatically update as commits are pushed. ---- --- 🚫 This PR disables script generation and caching for workflows containing conditional blocks to prevent issues with divergent execution paths. The change adds detection logic to identify conditional blocks in workflow definitions and skips script generation when found, with appropriate logging for both successful detection and error cases.
🔍 Detailed Analysis ### Key Changes - **Conditional Block Detection**: Added logic to inspect workflow definitions and identify conditional blocks using `get_all_blocks()` and `BlockType.CONDITIONAL` - **Script Generation Control**: Modified `generate_workflow_script()` to early return when conditional blocks are detected, preventing caching of potentially divergent paths - **Error Handling**: Implemented try-catch block around block inspection with fallback behavior and warning logging - **Logging Enhancement**: Added informational logging when conditional blocks are found and warning logging for inspection failures ### Technical Implementation ```mermaid flowchart TD A[generate_workflow_script called] --> B[Get all blocks from workflow definition] B --> C{Block inspection successful?} C -->|No| D[Log warning, continue with script generation] C -->|Yes| E{Has conditional blocks?} E -->|No| F[Continue with normal script generation] E -->|Yes| G[Log info message] G --> H[Return early - skip script generation] D --> F ``` ### Impact - **Cache Safety**: Prevents caching of scripts for workflows with conditional logic that could lead to incorrect cached results for different execution paths - **System Reliability**: Reduces potential bugs from cached scripts that don't account for conditional branching behavior - **Observability**: Provides clear logging to help developers understand when and why script generation is being skipped - **Graceful Degradation**: Continues normal operation if block inspection fails, ensuring system robustness

author: copilot
body:
Implements the Ψ-NS-GCV (Psi Navier-Stokes - Global Coherence Vector) theory formalization in Lean4, providing a mathematical framework for the 3D Navier-Stokes global regularity problem through quantum coherence field analysis.

## New QCAL Modules

- **`QCAL/Frequency.lean`**: Fundamental frequency constants (f₀ = 141.7001 Hz, ω₀, ω∞) with positivity proofs
- **`QCAL/NoeticField.lean`**: Quantum-classical coupling constants (γE, ζ', ε, ℏ, m)
- **`QCAL.lean`**: Root module for exports

## PsiNS_GCV Formalization

- **`Lean4-Formalization/PsiNSE/PsiNS_GCV.lean`**: Core formalization containing:
  - Ψ field definition: `Ψ(u)(x) = ‖∇u(x)‖²` (gradient energy density)
  - Master equation: `∂Ψ/∂t + ω∞² Ψ - ζ'π ΔΦ - RΨ = 0`
  - Quantum pressure correction: `Φ = ∇·u + (ℏ²/2m)(Δ√ρ/√ρ)`
  - Feedback term: `RΨ = 2ε cos(2πf₀t) ⟨∇u, ∇u⟩`
  - Main theorem `global_smooth_solution_exists` with proper typing

## Example

```lean
-- Initial data structure
structure InitialData where
  u₀ : VectorField
  h1 : u₀ ∈ H¹
  div_free : ∀ x, div u₀ x = 0

-- Main theorem: global smooth solutions exist with bounded gradient energy
theorem global_smooth_solution_exists (u₀ : InitialData) :
  ∃ u : ℝ × ℝ³ → ℝ³,
    (∀ t ≥ 0, (fun x ↦ u (t, x)) ∈ C_infinity ∩ L_infinity) ∧
    (∀ t ≥ 0, matrixNorm (grad (fun x ↦ u (t, x)) (0, 0, 0)) ^ 2 ≤ C₀)
```

## Implementation Notes

- Differential operators (div, grad, laplacian) use placeholder implementations with TODO comments for future Mathlib integration
- Main theorem uses `sorry` intentionally—proof framework to be completed via Ψ-field energy estimates
- QCAL modules have complete proofs (0 sorry statements)
- Test suite (`PsiNS_GCV_Tests.lean`) validates 28 structural components

## Documentation

- `PsiNS_GCV_README.md`: Mathematical framework and implementation details
- `PSI_NS_GCV_IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md`: Complete implementation summary
- Updated `Lean4-Formalization/README.md` with new modules

> ChatGPT Plus
> Psi Ns Lean4 Formalization
> · other
> -- Lean4 Formalization of Ψ–NS–GCV Theory
> -- Author: José Manuel Mota Burruezo (JMMB Ψ ✷)
> -- Date: 2025-12-07
> -- Description: Formal resolution of the Navier–Stokes Problem via Field Ψ coherence
> 
> 
> import Mathlib.Analysis.PDE
> import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.L2Space
> import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.InfiniteSum
> import Mathlib.Analysis.Fourier
> import QCAL.Frequency
> import QCAL.NoeticField
> 
> 
> namespace PsiNS
> 
> 
> open Real Set Topology
> 
> 
> noncomputable section
> 
> 
> -- Parameters and constants
> @[reducible] def f₀ : ℝ := 141.7001  -- fundamental frequency (Hz)
> @[reducible] def ω₀ : ℝ := 2 * π * f₀
> @[reducible] def ω∞ : ℝ := 2 * π * 888.0  -- peak coherent frequency (rad/s)
> @[reducible] def ζ' : ℝ := -0.207886  -- zeta'(1/2), empirical value
> @[reducible] def γE : ℝ := 0.5772     -- Euler–Mascheroni constant
> 
> 
> -- Initial data: divergence-free H¹ velocity field
> structure InitialData where
>   u₀ : ℝ³ → ℝ³
>   h1 : u₀ ∈ H¹(ℝ³)
>   div_free : ∀ x, div (u₀ x) = 0
> 
> 
> -- Field Ψ definition
> @[simp]
> def Psi (u : ℝ³ → ℝ³) : ℝ³ → ℝ := fun x ↦ ∥∇ u x∥²
> 
> 
> -- Master equation for Ψ field
> @[simp]
> def psiEqn (Ψ : ℝ³ → ℝ) (Φ : ℝ³ → ℝ) (RΨ : ℝ³ → ℝ) : ℝ³ → ℝ :=
>   fun x ↦ ∂Ψ/∂t x + ω∞^2 * Ψ x - ζ' * π * laplacian (Φ x) - RΨ x
> 
> 
> -- Quantum pressure correction term (Φ)
> @[simp]
> def Φ (ρ : ℝ³ → ℝ) : ℝ³ → ℝ := fun x ↦ div (u x) + ℏ^2 / (2 * m) * (laplacian (sqrt ρ x) / sqrt ρ x)
> 
> 
> -- Feedback nonlinear term RΨ
> @[simp]
> def RΨ (u : ℝ³ → ℝ³) (t : ℝ) : ℝ³ → ℝ := fun x ↦
>   2 * ε * Real.cos (2 * π * f₀ * t) * inner (∇ u x) (∇ u x / ∥u x∥)
> 
> 
> -- Main theorem: global regularity of solution

body:
CI fails on migration `20251203_add_postgis` because standard PostgreSQL image lacks PostGIS extension (ref: 802f4033226cd400e84ef432b99471e93fe6c8e4).

## Changes

- **Service image**: `postgres:15` → `postgis/postgis:15-3.3`
- **New step before migrations**: Install `postgresql-client`, wait for Postgres readiness, execute `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS postgis;`

```yaml
- name: Wait for Postgres and enable PostGIS
  env:
    PGPASSWORD: postgres
  run: |
    sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y postgresql-client
    until pg_isready -h localhost -p 5432 -U postgres; do sleep 1; done
    psql -h localhost -U postgres -d afrisense_test -c "CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS postgis;"
```

The PostGIS image ships with the extension binaries; explicit activation ensures it's available before Prisma applies spatial migrations.

Voir le run/job référencé (ref: 802f4033226cd400e84ef432b99471e93fe6c8e4).

## Summary by Sourcery

Normalize usernames to be lowercase and trimmed across user creation, updates, lookups, and existing data, and route auth flows through UsersService instead of accessing the User repository directly.

Bug Fixes:
- Ensure username-based lookups are case-insensitive by normalizing input usernames before querying.
- Prevent creation or update of users with usernames differing only by casing by consistently lowercasing stored usernames.

Enhancements:
- Introduce a shared username normalization helper in UsersService and apply it to create, update, and username-change operations.
- Refactor AuthService to depend on UsersService for user retrieval and updates instead of using the User repository directly.

Tests:
- Adjust AuthService unit tests to mock UsersService instead of the User repository.

Chores:
- Add a database migration to normalize all existing usernames to trimmed lowercase values.

Establishes ZVLI-2025-001, the foundational sovereignty guarantee document defining 12 principals that prevent vendor lock-in across all StrategicKhaos systems.

## Document Structure

**Core Principals** (with implementation specs and client guarantees):
- Data Portability: JSON/CSV/YAML export within 24h
- API Abstraction: Adapter pattern for all third-party integrations
- Infrastructure as Code: Terraform/K8s/Docker for reproducible deployments
- Knowledge Sovereignty: Markdown/Git for all documentation
- Identity Independence: Multi-provider auth with Keycloak fallback
- Financial Rails Diversity: 4-tier payment pathway redundancy
- Compute Portability: Container-based workloads, multi-cloud tested
- Communication Sovereignty: Matrix/Discord/Email/Satellite layered comms
- AI Model Interchangeability: Unified prompt schema (Claude↔GPT↔Grok↔local)
- Cryptographic Provenance: GPG signatures + OpenTimestamps for audit trails
- Source Code Ownership: GitHub + Gitea mirror + local bundles
- Observability Independence: Prometheus/Grafana/Elasticsearch stack

**Verification Framework**:
- Red/Blue/Purple team protocols for lock-in stress testing
- 4-tier certification (Bronze→Platinum) based on escape capability
- Antifragile audit requirements: vendor outage/acquisition/hostage scenarios

**Legal Compliance**:
- Attorney verification checklist (<24h export, tested migration plans)
- Client rights: export, migrate, self-host, audit, fork
- AI Board consensus signature block

Document placed in `legal/` alongside other governance instruments (TRUST_DECLARATION, NON_AGGRESSION_CLAUSE).

Note: "PRINCIPALS" spelling is intentional per requirements.

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

# ZERO VENDOR LOCK-IN PRINCIPALS

## StrategicKhaos Sovereignty Guarantee

**Document ID:** ZVLI-2025-001  
**Version:** 1.0  
**Effective Date:** December 7, 2025  
**Issuing Entity:** Strategickhaos DAO LLC (EIN 39-2900295)

---

## PURPOSE

This document establishes the **Zero Vendor Lock-in Principals** that govern all systems, software, and services developed under the StrategicKhaos ecosystem. These principals ensure that clients, partners, and the operator maintain complete control over their data, infrastructure, and operations—regardless of any vendor relationship changes.

---

## THE 12 SOVEREIGNTY PRINCIPALS

### Principal 1: DATA PORTABILITY

**Statement:**  
Every piece of data stored in any StrategicKhaos system can be exported to a universal, open format within 24 hours.

**Implementation:**
- All databases support JSON/CSV/YAML export
- No proprietary binary formats for critical data
- Export scripts maintained and tested quarterly
- Migration documentation for each system

**Client Guarantee:**  
You will never be trapped by our data structures.

---

### Principal 2: API ABSTRACTION

**Statement:**  
All external integrations use abstraction layers that allow backend replacement without frontend changes.

**Implementation:**
- Adapter pattern for all third-party services
- Interface contracts documented in OpenAPI/GraphQL
- Mock servers for testing without vendor dependencies
- Graceful fallback for service unavailability

**Client Guarantee:**  
If a vendor disappears tomorrow, your systems keep working.

---

### Principal 3: INFRASTRUCTURE AS CODE

**Statement:**  
Every deployment is reproducible from version-controlled source files.

**Implementation:**
- Terraform for cloud resources
- Docker Compose for local development
- Kubernetes manifests for production
- No manual console configurations

**Client Guarantee:**  
Your entire infrastructure can be rebuilt from scratch in hours, not months.

---

### Principal 4: KNOWLEDGE SOVEREIGNTY

**Statement:**  
All documentation, notes, and institutional knowledge exist in self-owned, portable formats.

**Implementation:**
- Obsidian vaults (Markdown) for documentation
- Git repositories for code and configs
- No knowledge locked in SaaS platforms
- Regular exports to multiple locations

**Client Guarantee:**  
Your team's knowledge belongs to you, not to a subscription.

---

### Principal 5: IDENTITY INDEPENDENCE

**Statement:**  
Authentication and authorization systems do not depend on a single identity provider.

**Implementation:**
- Keycloak for self-hosted identity
- Support for multiple OAuth providers
- Local authentication fallback
- No vendor-specific SSO dependencies

**Client Guarantee:**  
If Google/Microsoft/Okta has an outage, you can still log in.

---

### Principal 6: FINANCIAL RAILS DIVERSITY

**Statement:**  
Revenue collection and treasury operations use multiple independent pathways.

**Implementation:**
- Primary: Traditional banking (NFCU)
- Secondary: BaaS integration (Thread Bank)
- Tertiary: Payment processors (Stripe)
- Quaternary: Cryptocurrency rails

**Client Guarantee:**  
No single financial vendor can cut off your operations.

---

### Principal 7: COMPUTE PORTABILITY

**Statement:**  
All workloads run on standard containers deployable to any cloud or bare metal.

**Implementation:**
- Docker containers for all services
- Kubernetes for orchestration
- No cloud-specific services in critical path
- Multi-cloud tested (GCP, Azure, AWS, local)

**Client Guarantee:**  
You can move to a different cloud provider in a weekend.

---

### Principal 8: COMMUNICATION SOVEREIGNTY

**Statement:**  
Business communications do not depend on a single messaging platform.

**Implementation:**
- Primary: Matrix/Element (self-hosted)
- Fallback: Discord (operational)
- Backup: Email (Protonmail)
- Emergency: Satellite (Starshield/LoRa)

**Client Guarantee:**  
Slack/Discord outages don't stop your business.

---

### Principal 9: AI MODEL INTERCHANGEABILITY

**Statement:**  
AI integrations use standardized interfaces that swap models transparently.

**Implementation:**
- Unified prompt contract schema
- Claude ↔ GPT ↔ Grok ↔ Local LLM
- Ollama for self-hosted inference
- No vendor-specific fine-tuning in critical paths

**Client Guarantee:**  
OpenAI price increases? Switch to Claude. Anthropic down? Use local Qwen.

---

### Principal 10: CRYPTOGRAPHIC PROVENANCE

**Statement:**  
All significant decisions and state changes are timestamped and cryptographically signed.

**Implementation:**
- GPG signatures on all commits
- OpenTimestamps for blockchain anchoring
- Merkle trees for audit trails
- BLAKE3 hashing for integrity

**Client Guarantee:**  
Every decision has verifiable proof of when and by whom it was made.

---

### Principal 11: SOURCE CODE OWNERSHIP

**Statement:**  
Full repository mirrors exist independent of any single code hosting platform.

**Implementation:**
- Primary: GitHub (operational)

## Proposed change
<!--

  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.

Ecowtt products produce many rain count sensors, there are largely three types:
- Total sensors - lifetime accumulating
- Resetting sensors - resetting to zero in certain condition, e.g. daily or after 24h no rain
- Rolling window sensors - total for the last X period

Total sensors and resetting sensors should have state class of `TOTAL_INCREASING`, and the rolling window ones should have `MEASUREMENT` as their state class correspondingly.

Previously, the code only counted hourly sensors as rolling window sensors, and #155321 was raised because 24h sensors are also rolling window but the code didn't take that into consideration.

As described in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/157882#issuecomment-3623267683, #155358 by @ogruendel was raised to fix the above issue, however, it was done in a wrong approach by changing all resetting sensors to `TOTAL`, and subsequent PRs #155812 and #157409 are heading down the wrong way further by completely removing the state class, causing long-term statistics for those resetting sensors to be deleted.

This PR reverts the three aforementioned PRs, and tries to assign the right state class for all the sensors.

author: tmitchel2
body:
## Overview

This PR implements the design and architecture documentation for file-based storage with git merge compatibility as specified in issue #343.

## Changes

Created comprehensive design documentation in `docs/design/`:

### 1. File Format Design (`file-based-storage-format.md`)
- **JSON Lines (JSONL) format** for storing RDF triples
- One triple per line for git merge compatibility
- Detailed schema with examples
- Git merge scenarios and conflict handling
- Compatibility with existing `InMemoryRDFTripleStore`

### 2. Storage Structure Design (`file-based-storage-structure.md`)
- Directory structure with partitioned data files
- Secondary indexes (by-predicate, by-indexed-object)
- Metadata management
- File lifecycle operations (read, write, compaction)
- Concurrency and locking strategies
- Performance optimization techniques

### 3. Merge Strategy Documentation (`file-based-storage-merge-strategy.md`)
- Git configuration with `.gitattributes`
- Union merge strategy for automatic merging
- Detailed merge scenarios with examples
- Conflict resolution guidelines (timestamp-based, LWW)
- Merge validation procedures
- CLI merge helper tool specification

## Key Design Decisions

1. **JSONL Format**: Chosen for line-based git merging, human readability, and streaming performance
2. **Partition-per-file**: Enables parallel access and minimizes merge conflicts
3. **Sorted content**: Maximizes merge success and enables efficient lookups
4. **Timestamp-based resolution**: Provides deterministic conflict resolution
5. **Separate indexes**: Allows independent updates and rebuilds

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] File format documented and approved
- [x] Storage structure designed
- [x] Merge strategy documented

## Epic

Part of Epic #342 - File-Based Storage Implementation

## Next Steps

The design documents provide the foundation for:
- Issue #344: Core File-Based Storage Implementation
- Issue #349: Git Merge Support Implementation
- All subsequent implementation phases

Closes #343

author: seannijjar
body:
this change is only concerned with adding the necessary builder code to construct Z routers. Z routers are not enabled with this change. Note also that this change is not final. It does not incorporate the most optimal implementations for Z routers (e.g. it specifies 2 receiver channels for Z routers, even though they have only one). This will materialize as inefficient L1 usage, but should not limit functionality. Optimizations will be considered future work.

Some relatively large rework was done with the fabric builder flow to accommodate the required changes. At a very high level, the builder moves towards configuration driven construction: different router types are defined and in combination with the fabric topology, a `FabricRouterChannelMapping` is generated. This object defines how channels are organized/enumerated in a router. For example, specifying the sender and receiver channel counts, and which VC each one maps to. 

This is useful for enabling a more configurable fabric builder code base. Additionally, it is required since Z routers are the first time in the fabric code-base where one router can have a meaningfully different micro-architecture than other ones in the same fabric:
- different sender channel and receiver channel counts
- different sender -> receiver channel mapping
- different number of receiver -> downstream connections

### Important New Types
- RouterConnectionMapping: defines VC -> channel mappings per router (for externally exposed channels)
- IntermeshVCConfig: defines how intermesh VCs are managed across the full fabric

#### Enums:
- `RouterVariant`: specifies the high-level router type (MESH or Z_ROUTER)
- `IntermeshVCMode`: specifies how intermesh flows are implemented in the system:
  - DISABLED: no intermesh
  - EDGE_ONLY: Intermesh VC on edge nodes only (traffic sinks at mesh boundary), no additional hops after switch over mesh boundary
  - FULL_MESH: The intermesh VC spans the full mesh, but forces traffic to sink into the dest mesh. Hopping through intermediate meshes is not allowed
  - FULL_MESH_WITH_PASS_THROUGH: above, but routing through intermediate meshes is allowed
- `IntermeshRouterType`: defines how to implement a given intermesh router: Z mode or XY mode

### Note
To facilitate host side testing, a new component (`ConnectionRegistry`) was added. This was created purely for adding visibility into the fabric router builders for easier unit testing without device. This type was added to boot-strap this work but is now kept in place to simplify future change testing.

author: guihuaz
body:
## Fixes #222, #309, #574


### Description of the changes:
- add a helper function _snaprat to check if a result RAT should be zero with given precision. Apply _snaprat to addrat/subrat/lograt.
- The root causes of issues #222, #309, #574 are the same. For an irrational number result, the approximation introduces small errors beyond precision required, which is expected. The issue was Ratpak tried to take "precision" digits from the calculation result regardless where the result came from, and it exposed digits from approximation errors. Take `sqrt(2.25) - 1.5` for example. `sqrt(2.25)` might be approximated to `1.499...998...` depending on the precision. When this number subtracted `1.5`, the Ratpak got `0.000...001....` Ratpak took up to precision number of digits and converts to scientific format, which resulted `-1.2566515751494548126925332972115e-47`. This PR checks the magnitude difference between the result and the input operands. Since the result is too close to `47` magnitude smaller than original subtraction operands `1.499...998...` and `1.5`, it would be snapped to `0`.
- The same fix applies to `lograt` as well. 
- One further optimization could be a new sqrt function specifically checking perfect square first before using Taylor series approximation.

### How changes were validated:
<!--Review https://github.com/Microsoft/calculator/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md and ensure all contributing requirements are met.

Specify how you tested your changes (i.e. manual/ad-hoc testing, automated testing, new automated tests added)-->
- Add 1 test case in `CalculatorManagerTestStandard` to verify addrat. 
- Add 2 test cases in `CalculatorManagerTestScientific` to verify addrat and lograt
- Manual test the cases in the linked issues.
- Manual test log case: `log(sqrt(2.25)/1.5)`

* Enhanced the build script in `package.json` to display the contents of the `dist` directory after building for easier verification.
* Upgraded the `vite` dependency to version 5 and added `vite-plugin-vercel` for improved Vercel integration.

* Updated the description of "La Mansión de los Streamers" in `AboutSection.tsx` to refer to it as a "project" rather than a "reality show."

author: zeropath-ai[bot]
body:
The application fetches data from an external source using an insecure HTTP connection (`http://example.com/userdata`) and renders the response directly into the DOM using `innerHTML` without sanitization. This presents two critical risks:
1. **Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) Attack**: Because the request is unencrypted (HTTP), a network attacker can intercept and modify the response.
2. **Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)**: Since the application assigns the `responseText` directly to `innerHTML`, any malicious script injected by an attacker (via MITM or if the source endpoint is compromised) will be executed in the user's browser.
Additionally, if the main application is served over HTTPS, this request will trigger Mixed Content warnings or be blocked by the browser.

author: jackwotherspoon
body:
## Summary

Optimizes session summary generation by moving it from exit-time (blocking) to startup-time (non-blocking), eliminating the potential max of a 5 second delay when closing the CLI.

Previously, when a user exited the CLI, the application would block while making an API call to generate a summary for the current session. This caused a noticeable delay before the terminal returned to the user. Now, summary generation happens in the background on the *next* startup, making exit instant.

Also added a check that only generates a summary if more than 1 user messages exist in the session. This way non-interactive mode sessions are not summarized as well as single message sessions where the initial prompt most likely captures the overall intent of the user, saving model calls.

## Details

### Move summary generation from exit to startup
- Removed the blocking `await generateAndSaveSummary(config)` call from the cleanup handler in `AppContainer.tsx`
- Added a fire-and-forget `generateSummary(config).catch(...)` call in the startup `useEffect`
- Summary generation now runs in the background without blocking the UI or delaying startup

### Add summary generation to `--list-sessions`
- When running `gemini --list-sessions`, the CLI now checks if the most recent session needs a summary and generates one if so
- This ensures the session list shows an up-to-date summary for the previous session
- Uses a blocking call here since the user is explicitly viewing sessions and expects accurate data

### Use filename-based sorting instead of mtime
- Changed from sorting sessions by file modification time (`mtime`) to sorting by filename
- Session filenames contain creation timestamps (e.g., `session-2024-01-15T10-30-abc123.json`)
- This correctly identifies the most recently *created* session rather than the most recently *modified*
- Fixes edge case where resuming an old session would incorrectly mark it as "most recent" due to updated mtime

### Skip single message sessions (1+ user message threshold)
- Only generate summaries for sessions with  more than 1 user message
- Short sessions (like single non-interactive prompts) don't benefit from summaries - the first message already serves as a good description
- Reduces unnecessary API calls and helps users avoid hitting rate limits

### Code cleanup
- Removed redundant `dirExists` variable in `getPreviousSession`
- Removed `generateAndSaveFromCurrentSession` function (dead code after refactor)
- Simplified session finding logic to only check the most recent session file
- Switched from sync `fs` to async `fs/promises` for non-blocking I/O

## Files Changed

| File | Changes |
|------|---------|
| `packages/core/src/services/sessionSummaryUtils.ts` | Refactored `getPreviousSession` to use filename sorting and 5-message threshold; simplified `generateSummary` for fire-and-forget usage |
| `packages/core/src/services/sessionSummaryUtils.test.ts` | Updated tests for new behavior including message threshold and filename-based sorting |
| `packages/cli/src/ui/AppContainer.tsx` | Removed blocking exit call; added fire-and-forget startup call |
| `packages/cli/src/utils/sessions.ts` | Added `generateSummary` call before listing sessions |
| `packages/cli/src/utils/sessions.test.ts` | Added mock for `generateSummary` |

## Testing

- All existing tests updated and passing
- New test cases added for:
  - Filename-based session ordering
  - Sessions with 0 or 1 message returning null

author: marcprux
body:
`followSymlinkInits` is failing on an Android emulator (API 28 and 35). See https://github.com/swift-android-sdk/swift-android-sdk-workflow-demo/actions/runs/20010192707/job/57378485958#step:22:1657 :

```
Test followSymlinkInits() recorded an issue at StatTests.swift:121:7: Expectation failed: (symlinkStat.sizeAllocated → 8192) < (targetStat.sizeAllocated → 8192)
```

I can also reproduce it locally with `skip android test`.

I *believe* this is a known limitation of symbolic links on Android.

Note that the Android CI in https://github.com/swiftlang/github-workflows only builds and doesn't (yet) test, so this wasn't caught in the checks that were added in https://github.com/apple/swift-system/pull/270.

This PR allow to use an IP address in the configuration of the P1 sensor.
This sensor can be a HA sensor or the IP address of a Zendure 3CT, Shelly 3EM, Shelly 3EM Pro or Shelly 3EM-63.
The communication with these smart meters are direct HTTP GET commands and will be polled with a refresh rate of 1 second.
The P1 sensor is shown in the Zendure Manager

author: frederikfabriciusbjerre
body:
## Add ADMG Support

### Summary

- **New graph class**: `ADMG` is now a first-class graph type alongside DAG, PDAG, and UG
- **M-separation**: Generalization of d-separation for graphs with bidirected edges
- **Adjustment sets**: Implementation of the Generalized Adjustment Criterion for ADMGs
- **Typed error handling**: Improved error types across all graph classes (DAG, PDAG, UG, ADMG)

### New R Functions

| Function | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `is_admg()` | Check if a graph is a valid ADMG |
| `spouses()` | Get nodes connected via bidirected edges |
| `districts()` | Get c-components (maximal bidirected-connected sets) |
| `m_separated()` | Test m-separation between node sets |
| `is_valid_adjustment_admg()` | Check if a set is valid for causal adjustment |
| `all_adjustment_sets_admg()` | Enumerate all valid adjustment sets |

### Additional Changes

- `as_adjacency()` and `as_igraph()` now support bidirected edges
- `caugi()` constructor accepts `class = "ADMG"`
- `as_caugi()` supports conversion to ADMG
- Improved error messages throughout (e.g., "Self-loops not allowed" instead of "self-loops")

Fixes #22
